entities.name: Monica Alvarez
entities.description:
Monica is one of several protagonists of the IDW Publishing comic series Jurassic Park: The Devils in the Desert.

Monica Alvarez was born Monica Ramirez to Dr. Jorge Ramirez and an unknown woman. Like her father, Monica pursued working in the field of paleontology - the study of prehistoric lifeforms such as dinosaurs. Monica would become an expert in her field and work alongside her father at a California State University.

At some point before 2008, Monica met and married a Steven Alvarez and took his last name. Alvarez was an engineer and part of the United States Armed Forces in Afghanistan. According to Monica, Steven was uninterested in her field. For eighteen months (from 2007-2008) Steven had stayed in an unnamed Afghan village helping to improve the infrastructure of the area. Even building a school, a hospital, and improving the road network. The village however didn't tell the Americans about a bomb buried by the Taliban and let it detonate, killing Steven and six other American G.I.'s.

Even three years after his passing Monica kept Steven's surname.

entities.name: Violet Moody
entities.description:
Violet Moody is one of few Maisie Lockwood's friends, they met at the campsite run by the former's grandparents, during the time when Claire, Owen and Maisie kept a low profile after the events at Lockwood Manor.

At age 12, Maisie and her parents went to a campsite called "Happy Trail" where they would spend three weeks while remaining fugitives. Maisie and her parents were taking a walk by the blue lake in the area, she met a group of kids her age who were coming out of the forest towards the lake, among this group was Violet, who is revealed to be the granddaughter of the administrators. of the campsite. After talking a little, Maisie shows Violet her drawings of dinosaurs, feeling impressed by the detail these portraits had compared to what dinosaurs looked like in real life. A little later, Violet heads into the forest, Maisie follows her encountering a pair of Triceratops, Tri and Pi. Violet reveals that she and her friends had recently found these dinosaurs and were trying to help them get to Fenders Rock so they wouldn't run the risk of being hunted.

Violet and Maisie spent more time together, talking about finding a way to help Tri and Pi.

One day, Owen and Claire go to a meeting so Maisie stays with Violet and her grandmother, there the blonde reveals that her parents died when she was little and that is why she lived with her grandparents. They discover two poachers, Jones and Macnally, who were looking to hunt Blue and other dinosaurs. After a series of problems, Maisie discovers that her parents cannot return in time, so Violet, Maisie and their friends decide to make a plan to save the Triceratops and stop the hunters. Using water balloons and other traps, the hunters are outwitted by Violet, Maisie and their friends. However, Violet is caught by Jones, who threatens her to find out where the animals were. Blue intervenes and causes the defeat of Jones, the raptor watches Violet with unknown intentions, Maisie saves her friend and manages to place a tracker on Blue so that she can be located another time.

entities.name: Oscar Morales
entities.description:
Oscar Morales was one of the InGen mercenaries in Jurassic Park: The Game.

Oscar is one of a number of mercenaries retained by the InGen corporation. Twelve years prior to the events that unfolded in the first movie he was hired, along with many other mercenaries, to "remove" the native people on Isla Nublar after it's purchase by InGen from the Costa Rican government. This was done so that the island could be converted into Jurassic Park without the security or liability concerns of having an existing population.

Oscar killed some of the indigenous people who tried to resist the relocation, an act which Nima views as murder leading her to despise him. However when discussing the matter afterward Oscar seemed to feel remorse for his actions toward the civilian population of Isla Nublar recognizing it as an immoral act on his part. To remind himself of those people who either died for him or were killed by him, Oscar had a sleeve of tattoos inked onto his left arm; the gravestones symbolizing his friends who died for him and the skulls symbolizing the enemies he had killed.

Oscar and his young comrade Billy Yoder, arrive by helicopter to Isla Nublar as part of an operation by InGen to extract remain personnel trapped on the island. After they found the survivors, they had multiple confrontations with the many carnivores that roamed the island. Oscar was already a skilled fighter and brave in the face of peril, as evidenced by engaging in one-to-one combat with a Velociraptor and succeeding in killing it as well as scarring the alpha-female. He also seemed to have good knowledge of the names of the dinosaurs on the island, seen when correcting Billy Yoder from calling a Pteranodon a Pterodactyl.

entities.name: Mr. DNA
entities.description:
Mr. DNA was a cartoon character designed to explain to Jurassic Park tourists, who are assumed to be laymen, how InGen recreated the dinosaurs.

He was an anthropomorphic DNA helix with arms, legs, and a face. He was created solely for the movie and never appeared in the novels.

Mr. DNA was created by InGen to help visitors understand the processes involved in the creation of the dinosaurs on Jurassic Park. A film starring him and InGen's founder John Hammond would be played in a theater located in the park's Visitor Center before a tour. Mr. DNA also was used on the maintenance board of Jurassic Park's Geothermal Power Plant and on a board telling how tall a person must be to ride the upcoming Bone Shaker roller coaster.

After the Jurassic Park Incident the cartoon character seemed to have been put out of service by his company for about a decade.

entities.name: Mr. Gold
entities.description:
Mr. Gold was a minor antagonist in season 5 of Jurassic World: Camp Cretaceous. Mr. Gold was one of the investors who came to Mantah Corp Island to meet with Daniel Kon alongside Cyrus and Lana Molina to see dino fights.

Mr. Gold, Molina, and Cyrus arrive on Mantah Corp Island and are greeted by Kon, Mr. Gold asks why he took their phones, Kon says he can find a way to keep them entertained without their phones, Kon then brings them to the compound. Molina asks for his name, to which he says she can call him "Mr. Gold", she then gives him her card. When Kon brings his son, Kenji to the party, Mr. Gold quickly catches on that they are family and states he can't see the relation. They then hear Little Eatie roar, and Kon says he's just whetting their appetite for tomorrow, so they continue their conversation and listen to Kenji's stories of how he survived so many dinosaur encounters.

While walking to the Redwood forest for the presentation, Mr. Gold and Molina both get annoyed about how long its taking and request easier modes of transportation. Kash then arrives to join the presentation, so Kenji brings Mr. Gold and the other investors through the airlock while Kon talks to him. During the Presentation, Mr. Gold took control of Big Eatie. He caused her to fight against the Spinosaurus and 2 Velociraptors. When the Nublar Six, minus Kenji, came to stop the dino fights, he used Big Eatie to chase after them. This gave Darius Bowman and Brooklynn the opportunity to disrupt the control chip in her head and free her from his mind control. After she escaped, Big Eatie ran off, stepping on and crushing Mr. Gold.

Mr. Gold, a man of mystery, exudes a calm and collected demeanor. While he's impressed by Kenji's potential, his reluctance to reveal his identity to Lana Molina hints at a darker side. His obsession with protecting his assets and his keen interest in the dinosaurs' potential suggest a calculating mind. However, his true, heartless nature is exposed when he attempts to kill innocent children, revealing a disturbing lack of empathy.

entities.name: Mr. Gutierrez
entities.description:
Mr. Gutierrez is the father of Sammy Gutierrez. He and his family provided the meat for the carnivores of Jurassic World. When Mantah Corp requested to send his daughter to spy and steal dinosaur DNA for them, Mr. Gutierrez and his wife refused to use their daughter that way, but Sammy agreed to prevent their family from losing the ranch. They didn't know what she did until she went to Isla Nublar.

After the Jurassic World incident, Mr. Gutierrez and his family now provide meat for Mantah Corp Island, although they do not know where they are taking them. At the end Mr. Gutierrez is seen reuniting with his daughter and was surprised but happy to see that she and Yasmina are a couple. Two years later, Sammy and her family continue to provide the meat, for Mantah Corp's Island now as the "Secret Island".

Six years after the Jurassic World Incident in Jurassic World: Chaos Theory Sammy mentions that her family does not speak with her which includes Mr. Gutierrez. Lewis Dodgson later reveals that he made a deal with Gutierrez ranch and Sammy explains to Kenji that after the fallout from Masrani and Mantah Corp, the money Dodgson offered was too good for her parents to pass up. As Sammy knew that Biosyn wasn't trustworthy, she and her parents fought about it, culminating in Sammy's family not talking to her.

Following the Biosyn Incident, Sammy begins to reconcile with her parents, although things are still hard between them.

entities.name: Nyasasaurus
entities.description:
is a genus of archosaur from the Middle Triassic that may be the earliest known dinosaur. Its fossils were discovered in the Manda Formation of Tanzania during the 1930s. However, it would be described in 1956 by an English paleontologist, and formally in 2013. A name formelly coined for this prehistoric animal is Thecodontosaurus in 1932. The oldest record of dinosaurs was previously from the Carnian stage (the late Triassic period) in Argentina (Eoraptor, Herrerasaurus). Nyasasaurus predates this by around 12 million years earlier. A study mentions the similarity between the presacral vertebrae of Nyasasaurus and .

The name comes from near where it was discovered, Lake Nyasa. It is also located near the village of Gingama. The Manda Formation is inhabited by cynodonts, dicynodonts, archosaurs, amphibians, lungfish, and even a shark. The diet of Nyasasaurus is unknown, but being the possible earliest dinosauriform, scientists suggest that it was an omnivore.

Nyasasaurus is mentioned in the Jurassic World Annual 2016 during one of the facts about dinosaurs.

entities.name: Protoavis
entities.description:
(meaning "first bird") is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in Texas during the Late Triassic period. Some scientists think that Protoavis was the first bird, but others believe that the fossils associated with this species are actually several specimens mixed together. This little creature is known only from the incomplete remains of two individuals. Just enough was found to make some scientists believe that this animal may be at the base of the bird family tree.

Scientists are in the process of comparing the remains of Protoavis with other well-known theropod, such as Troodon, and are comparing similarities and differences. It has also been suggested that Protoavis is not closely associated with birds, but rather that this small creature may have been a very early theropod.

Protoavis appeared in the website Jurassic Park Institute on Dinopedia.

Protoavis is mentioned in one of Mr. DNA's Dino Trivias, stating that it may be the first ever bird.

entities.name: Abelisaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Abel's lizard") is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur. Abelisaurus, which lived in South America (specifically Argentina or officially the Argentine Republic) during the Late Cretaceous, was a member of the Abelisauridae family, which had powerful jaws and tiny forelimbs. In most illustrations it has three long fingers and long forelimbs, but in reality this dinosaur had four and tiny forelimbs.

In the Lockwood Manor, on the first floor, there was a diorama with a Dracorex in a savannah, saving its egg from a group of seven Abelisaurus. However, it is worth noting that Abelisaurus lived in South America, while Dracorex lived in North America, so this ecological interaction never occurred in life.

During the events of 2022, Abelisaurus was seen on the CIA's Black Market tracker list, implying that it was cloned sometime prior to 2022, and was roaming free across the USA (or at least, roaming within the black markets) during that year.

By 2027, however, any Abelisaurus that were cloned were faced with the threat of re-extinction. The planet's modern-day climate proved lethal for dinosauris, causing many species of to begin to die out. However, this is with the exception of those in tropical regions, as these regions best resemble the climate of the Mesozoic. Due to this, and the fact that whether or not it was cloned is still also unconfirmed, the fate of Abelisaurus remains unknown by the time of Jurassic World: Rebirth.

entities.name: Abrictosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "wakeful lizard") is a genus of heterodontosaurid dinosaur that lived in southern Africa (in countries like Lesotho and South Africa) during the Early Jurassic period. It provides more evidence that dinosaurs originated in or near what is now South America. It would have walked on its hind legs and been a swift runner. Although the fossils were discovered in South Africa, scientists know that this region was once attached to South America during the Jurassic Period. Paleontologists think that the dinosaurs spread out all over the region by migration, a type of travel that spreads animals to different parts of the world. So far, the earliest dinosaur fossils have been discovered in South America and the surrounding lands that were connected to it during the Early Mesozoic (until the discovery of Nyasasaurus on the continent of Africa).

What scientists know of Abrictosaurus comes mostly from the skull fragments of a single specimen. This specimen is believed to be a female of the genus Heterodontosaurus. It is believed to be of this genus because it possesses similar dentition, although it lacks large canines.

Abrictosaurus appeared on Jurassic Park Institute now archived on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Acanthopholis
entities.description:
(meaning “spiny scales”) is an extinct genus of Nodosauridae dinosaur that lived in England during the Late Cretaceous period. The armor of Acanthopholis consisted of oval keeled plates set almost horizontally into the skin, with long spikes protruding from the neck and shoulder area, along the spine. Named by Thomas Huxley in 1867, one of the most prominent scientists and thinkers of 19th century Europe, Acanthopholis has had a somewhat controversial history. It was probably slightly smaller and lighter than its North American nodosaur relatives.

Acanthopholis was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Achelousaurus
entities.description:
(meaning “Achelous's lizard”) is a extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceratopsian ceratopsian] from the same family as Centrosaurus that lived in Montana during the Late Cretaceous period 74.2 million years ago. It is a relative of another frilled ceratopsian dinosaur, Pachyrhinosaurus. They shared the same strange lump of bone on their nose, called a boss. This bony lump was positioned where other frilled dinosaurs, like Triceratops, had their nose horns.

Achelousaurus was a fairly large plant-eating dinosaur that looked similar in body type to the other larger members of its North American family. There is ongoing discussion as to whether this dinosaur warrants its own genus. There seems to be ongoing speculation that it is a species of Pachyrhinosaurus, perhaps showing gender differentiation. Most likely, it will take a more complete specimen to settle the debate. It is at present considered by many to be somewhere between the Pachyrhinosaurus and Einiosaurus.

Achelousaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Acheroraptor
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in modern-day Montana (USA) during the Late Cretaceous period 72.6 million years ago. Its fossils have been found in the famous Hell Creek Formation, home to Tyrannosaurus and another raptor, Dakotaraptor.

Acheroraptor is mentioned in the Jurassic World Dinosaur Field Guide as being a predator of Edmontosaurus, Pachycephalosaurus, and Thescelosaurus. In reality, while it's possible Acheroraptors did infact hunt the latter 2, adult Edmontosaurus would have been too large for even packs of Acheroraptors to take them down.

entities.name: Achillobator
entities.description:
(meaning "Achilles hero") is an extinct genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Asia (specifically Mongolia) during the Late Cretaceous period around 96-89 million years ago. It is named after the Greek mythological hero Achilles, who has been known as the greatest of all the Greek warriors.

Achillobator was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Achillobator was released a part of the Jurassic World: Rebirth toyline as a Strike Attack figure.

Achillobator is one of the many raptor species that were mentioned on a plaque display.

entities.name: Acrocanthosaurus
entities.description:
Acrocanthosaurus is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Early Cretaceous period, with a particularly tall spine column, giving it a similar appearance to the of the same time period and even to the point where people believed it was a spinosaurid. Unlike spinosaurids, who were riverine hunters with semi-aquatic hunting behaviors, Acrocanthosaurus was a heavily built predator that preferred slow moving prey and carrion over other meat. The footprints of Acrocanthosaurus can be seen publicly in Glen Rose, Texas. A complete skeleton is on display in Idabel, Oklahoma. Acrocanthosaurus was once classified as a spinosaurid, but it was reclassified as a carcharodontosaurid. Though most paleontologists agree the bone structure on Acrocanthosauruss back supported a sail, some theorize it was a hump of fat like that of a camel. Acrocanthosaurus gained fame for hunting large sauropods like Astrodon and Sauroposeidon alone. To back this theory up there are footprints of a Acrocanthosaurus right along side of an Astrodons footprints.

Acrocanthosaurus is one of the many dinosaurs that appeared in the browsing section of Dinopedia in the Jurassic Park Institute.

Acrocanthosaurus was featured in early conpect art of Jurassic World: Camp Cretaceous. Acrocanthosaurus was one of the candidate creatures for a companion that the campers would have, with another being Cryolophosaurus . This role would ultimately go to Bumpy the Ankylosaurus in the final product.

entities.name: Adasaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "evil lizard") is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. Scientists believe that it was small and lightweight. It also had a killer claw like Velociraptor, but the claw was smaller.

What we do know from the few fossils that have been discovered so far, is that Adasaurus was a small, meat-eating dinosaur that was very lightweight and had many bird-like features. It has been placed in the same family as Velociraptor for now, but future discoveries may change that.

This small dinosaur adds fuel to the ever-growing debate surrounding dinosaurs and birds. Adasaurus has been described as being extremely similar to Archaeopteryx. It has enough of the dromaeosaur characteristics to be placed in that family too, but the overall view of those types of raptors is evolving into their being referred to as bird-like dinosaurs, complete with feathers. Eventually, some members of that family may be reclassified as birds instead of dinosaurs.

Adasaurus appeared on the website Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its artwork, it is shown catching a lizard before eating it.

entities.name: Aegyptosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in Africa during the Late Cretaceous period around 100-94 million years ago. It lived along the shores of an ancient sea in what is now the Sahara Desert. This large dinosaur is actually a smaller relative of the gigantic Argentinosaurus from South America. During the time Aegyptosaurus lived, Africa and South America were still connected and it may have moved to this North African location over many thousands of years, involving into a smaller version of their South American relatives, though this is debated.

Aegyptosaurus is yet another spectacular specimen temporarily lost during WWII. Discovered in the same location as Spinosaurus, it may have been lost in the same bombing of Germany that may have destroyed evidence of other specimens.

Aegyptosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Aeolosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period. Although it was small for a titanosaur, it was still quite large, and like some of the other smaller titanosaurs, it had bony plates on its back to protect it from the bite of large predators that would have attacked from above.

Known from several partial skeletons, Aeolosaurus is the first known titanosaur from fossil-rich Patagonia to exhibit dermal plates. An interesting note is that unusually thick egg shells with strange dome shapes on the surface were found associated with this dinosaur's fossil material.

Aeolosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown repelling two unknown dromaeosaur theropods.

entities.name: Afrovenator
entities.description:
is a genus of megalosaurid theropod that lived in North Africa during the Middle Jurassic period. It was the first almost complete skeleton found of a large African meat-eating dinosaur. It was unearthed in 1993 by an amateur fossil hunter who was on a National Geographic-sponsored expedition. This dinosaur was medium-sized and built for a life of active hunting, with long, strong back legs and large, strong arms designed for catching and holding its prey.

Afrovenator appears to be descended from earlier dinosaurs such as Megalosaurus. As this family was widely spread through ancient Europe and South America, it is not surprising that a relation would also have lived in Africa as its ancestors may have passed through. The only major Afrovenator parts missing from the type specimen are most of the lower jaw, the nose, some ribs and vertebrae, and toe bones. All in all, it is a remarkably complete specimen.

Afrovenator was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Afrovenator was one of the dinosaurs featured in an Jurassic World Survival update in Jurassic World Play.

entities.name: Agilisaurus
entities.description:
is a genus of ornithischian dinosaur that lived in China during the Middle Jurassic period. Being very lightly built, its long legs could carry it through the forests very quickly, giving it the ability to escape from all kinds of predators.

The Agilisaurus type specimen was found while construction crews were digging the foundation of the Zigong Dinosaur Museum in the Sichuan Province of China. It was an almost complete skeleton, and as a result of this discovery, another early Chinese ornithopod was reclassified to this genus.

This is the most complete ornithopod ever found in China. These small herbivores eventually evolved into the iguanodonts and hadrosaurs of the Cretaceous.

Agilisaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Agujaceratops
entities.description:
(meaning "Horned face from Aguja") is a genus of herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur. It is a chasmosaurine ceratopsian which lived during the Late Cretaceous period (late Campanian stage) in what is now Texas. Originally known as Chasmosaurus mariscalensis and described by Lehman in 1989, it was moved to a new genus by Lucas, Sullivan and Hunt in 2006. Lehman felt the habitat Agujaceratops lived in (at least where the fossil material was found) may have been a swamp, due to the nature of the sediments. Lehman, Wick & Barnes (2016) described a second species, Agujaceratops mavericus.

The skull displayed in Lockwood Manor appears to be a mix of Agujaceratops and another genus. While the plaque digitally displayed Agujaceratops, production designer Andy Nicholson confirmed it was one of two they combined to create a new, fictional genus.

The hybrid dinosaur Indoraptor, while fighting Blue the Velociraptor on the glass roof above the skull, falls on the skull and dies from being impaled on the horns.

entities.name: Agustinia
entities.description:
is a genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period in Argentina, South America. Its name honors the student Agustin Martinelli, who discovered the skeleton in 1997 and was part of the excavation team of the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales. At first, it initially has spikes on its back for defense and belonged to its own family, Agustiniidae. However, recent studies show that the spikes are now thought to be ribcage parts while the sauropod actually comes from the family branch of Rebbachisaurus.

Agustinia lived in the Lohan Cura Formation, which housed turtles and other sauropods.

Agustinia so far appeared in an artwork of the Dinopedia of the Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. However, it would receive a profile in the website Dinosaur Earth on Dinopedia.

It is portrayed in an outdated manner, with spikes on its back that are now believed to have been ribcage parts.

entities.name: Alamosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Ojo Alamo lizard") was an American titanosaur, found in Texas and named after Ojo Alamo - a formation in Texas where it was first discovered. It was the last and largest sauropod known from North America and may well have been prey to Tyrannosaurus. The name Alamosaurus means "lizard from the Alamo". One of the last sauropod dinosaurs, the largest individual is about 26 meters long and weighs 38 tons, rivaling the size of other titanic sauropods such as Argentinosaurus.

A skeleton of Alamosaurus stood in what was once the Visitor Center of the original Jurassic Park, along with a neighboring Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton. Alan, Ellie, Lex, and Tim attempted to use it to climb down from the ceiling to escape a member of the Velociraptor pack, whose attack caused the skeleton to fall apart.

Alamosaurus was referred on the inactive species list of Isla Adventura. However, it is revealed that a population of Alamosaurus have existed on Isla Sorna.

When the Visitor Center appears in other Jurassic Park media, Alamosaurus is often replaced by diplodocid sauropods such as Apatosaurus (LEGO Jurassic World) or Brontosaurus (Jurassic Park Discovery Center).

entities.name: Alaskacephale
entities.description:
(meaning "Alaska's head) is a genus of pachycephalosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alaska, United States. Being found in the Prince Creek formation alongside Edmontosaurus and Pachyrhinosaurus, it is known for being one of the few known Arctic dinosaurs as well as being an Arctic pachycephalosaur. According to the dimensions from the dinosaur's holotype, Alaskacephale was about half the size of Pachycephalosaurus or three-quarters the size of Prenocephale. It was also about the same size as Sphaerotholus. The closest relatives of Alaskacephale are Pachycephalosaurus and Stygimoloch.

Alaskacephale was featured (not by name) in an article about comparitive vertebrate taphonomy of boned beds in Alaska in the Foundation Grants section of Jurassic Park Institute.

entities.name: Albertosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Horseshoe canyon formation between 71 and 68 million years ago in the Late Cretaceous period. Related and physically similar to its larger and more famous cousin Tyrannosaurus, albeit smaller, faster, and more slender in comparison, Albertosaurus could attain a length of 9 to 10 meters (30–33 feet) and a height of 3-3.6 meters (10–12 feet). It weighed about 3–4.4 tons. At one time, the related genus Gorgosaurus, another tyrannosaurid, was thought to be a species of Albertosaurus, but now they are usually considered two separate genera. Albertosaurus was one of top predators of its habitat as it had a big number of plant eaters to feed on, especially ceratopsians like Anchiceratops or Pachyrhinosaurus, or hadrosaurs like Saurolophus or Hypacrosaurus. There is also fossil evidence that this large, ferocious predator may have hunted in packs to bring down too large of prey such as Edmontosaurus. Albertosaurus also had a more slender skull and bones than other tyrannosaurs, making it a slim yet graceful deadly predator. Additionally, some paleontologists have speculated that Albertosaurus could run as fast as 30 mph.

Albertosaurus appeared on the website Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Albertosaurus made its first appearance in the video game Jurassic Park: Trespasser. It can kill Anne with a single bite.

Only 3 Albertosaurus are present in the final game; the first time it is seen is after a fall from a cliff in 'Industrial Jungle', hunting for Parasaurolophus alongside several Velociraptor. The other two Albertosaurus are located in the first 'Ascent' level. The first Albertosaurus can be killed with a machine gun mounted to a wrecked truck, and the second and third Albertosaurus can be dispatched with the toxic gun, a weapon that can bring the animal down with only a single shot.

entities.name: Alectrosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. It was only about half the size of T. rex and it was more lightly built, closer to Albertosaurus. It was about 20 feet long and had a mouth full of large, razor-sharp teeth that would have made this a pretty ferocious animal.

Alectrosaurus was discovered in 1923 during one of the American Museum of Natural History expeditions to China led by Roy Chapman Andrews. It was described in 1933 and re-described in 1989. It is considered to be a typical tyrannosaur family member and may in fact be a direct ancestor of Tarbosaurus.

Not much of this dinosaur has been found, and some of the fossils that were originally thought to belong to Alectrosaurus were later determined to belong to another dinosaur (an unknown species of therizinosaur, to be precise).

Alectrosaurus appeared on the website Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Aletopelta
entities.description:
is a genus of ankylosaurid that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now southern California. The skeleton was discovered in 1987 during a construction work near Carlsbad. The specimen was taken to the San Diego Museum of Natural History, where it was dubbed the "Carlsbad Ankylosaur". It was fully named in 2001 by James Kirkland and Tracy Lee Ford. The skeleton comes from the Point Loma Formation, which was part of the ocean during the Cretaceous. This means that Aletopleta was washed up shore and was scavenged by marine animals like Cretoxyrhina. Another dinosaur from the formation is an undetermined hadrosaur that could be Lambeosaurus or Saurolophus.

The discovery of Aletopelta is mentioned in the entry for the San Diego Museum of Natural History, within the museum guide of Jurassic Park Institute. The dinosaur isn't called by name, but rather identified as "Nodosaur".

entities.name: Algoasaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in South Africa during the Early Cretaceous period. It was found in the Kirkwood Formation, which is home to other dinosaurs such as sauropods, Paranthodon, Iyuku, and Nqwebasaurus. Discovered in a rock quarry in 1903, the workman didn't realize the importance of the find and they destroyed the fossils and used most of them to make bricks! The few bones that were saved showed that this dinosaur might be related to Apatosaurus or maybe the huge Argentinosaurus.

Algoasaurus has never officially been described. Its location in South Africa suggests that it may be related to the titanosaurs, but bone similarities seem to place it closer to the diplodocids.

Algoasaurus appeared on the website Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. Its artwork is a flipped and recolored Bellusaurus.

entities.name: Alioramus
entities.description:
("different branch") is an extinct genus of tyrannosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous period of Asia. The type species, A. remotus, is known from a partial skull and three foot bones recovered from Mongolian sediments which were deposited in a humid floodplain about 70 million years ago. These remains were named and described by Soviet paleontologist Sergei Kurzanov in 1976. A second species, A. altai, known from a much more complete skeleton, was named and described by Stephen L. Brusatte and colleagues Gregory M, Erickson, Regan A. Bever, Thomas D. Carr and Mark A. Norell in 2009. Its relationships to other tyrannosaurid genera are unclear, with some evidence supporting a hypothesis that Alioramus is closely related to the contemporary species Tarbosaurus bataar.

Alioramus were bipedal like all known theropods, and their sharp teeth indicate that they were carnivores. Known specimens were smaller than other tyrannosaurids like Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus rex, but their adult size is difficult to estimate since both species are known only from juvenile or sub-adult remains. The recent discovery of Qianzhousaurus indicates that it belongs to a distinct branch of tyrannosaur. The genus Alioramus is characterized by a row of 5 bony crests along the top of the snout, a greater number of teeth than any other genus of tyrannosaurid, and a lower skull than other tyrannosaurids.

Alioramus appeared in the website Jurassic Park Institute on Dinopedia.

Alioramus is one of the created dinosaurs that could be found in the nursery of the Jurassic Park Discovery Center.

entities.name: Allosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "different lizard") is an extinct genus of large theropod dinosaur from Europe and North America. Allosaurus was one of the most common predators of the Late Jurassic period and among the most dangerous. Like most theropod dinosaurs, its jaws were filled with sharp serrated teeth shaped like blades. Computer studies suggest that Allosaurus attacked by using its upper jaw like a machete to hack at its victim, then it used its lower jaw to bite out a slice of meat, although recent studies have proven this unlikely. In terms of size, it was the second-largest theropod of its era; only the likes of the megalosaurid Torvosaurus (10-11 meters or 33-36 feet with 4-5 tons of weight behind it). It averaged around 8.5 meters long (28 feet) and around 3 meters (10 feet) tall. However fragmentary remains suggest larger lengths of 11 to 12 meters (36-39 feet). Allosaurs top speed is estimated at 19 to 34 mph. It is thought that when hunting in groups they lacked "pack" cohesion. Fossils discovered are often riddled with broken bones, that later healed.

It might have been easy for an Allosaurus to kill a fairly defenseless dinosaur, like Camptosaurus, but Stegosaurus could certainly fight back with a blow from its tail. Thus it is thought that the Allosaurus hunted in large hunting gangs, similar to that of the Komodo dragon. While this means they hunted 'together', it was still every Allosaurus for itself. Often at times, an entire gang of these dinosaurs would be killed by their prey or by natural hazards, showing they had poor group coordination. They use their jaw to "hack" into prey like a battle axe.

It is known that Allosaurus led a dangerous life. The Allosaurus on display at the Smithsonian Institute has a smashed shoulder blade, several broken ribs, and a lower jaw so damaged that paleontologists didn't realize it was an Allosaurus jaw for over 100 years. But these were tough dinosaurs: Their bones show that they likely lived long enough for their wounds to heal. This Allosaur could very be the adolescent Big Al, whom was the main Allosaur in the 2000 Walking with Dinosaurs special . Big Al was known to be the most well preserved Allosaur's specimen to have ever been found. His skeleton is housed in the University of Wyoming campus. Big Al Two was the most complete Allosaur fossil.

Interestingly, unlike the rest of InGen's cloned theropods, the wrists of the adult Allosaurus are not pronated, though juveniles do have pronated wrists. Regardless, the cloned Allosaurus have a thicker head than in real life, and is slightly oversized, being 10.4 meters (34 feet) instead of 9.7 meters (32 feet). Adults have exaggerated crests and spines running down their backs. Female Allosaurus clones are mostly dark greyish blue with a yellow underbelly, a white stripe running from a patch around the eyes down the neck, and a pink tongue while the males are mostly dark blueish-grey with yellow underbellies, yellow stripes on the face and neck, a yellow circle around its eye orbit, white markings, and faded red on their crests, and a blue tongue.

entities.name: Alpha 06
entities.description:
Alpha 06 is a dinosaur boss from Jurassic World: The Game. It is a light grey Tyrannosaurus rex that looks almost like a Lythronax with orange bone-like spikes running down its back, as well as orange claws and flame like veins flowing through its body. It is capable of pulsing electricity when it attacks, steps, roars, or gets up. It is unknown if Alpha 06 is a hybrid or a genetically enhanced T. rex. It does, however, look very similar to Omega 09.

Alpha 06 was added to the game on October 27th, 2017, as an area boss carnivore for Halloween.

Alpha 06 begins with 4,596 HP and 209 damage per hit, the same as Omega 09. Each time it is beaten, it revives with doubled HP and damage. This cycle will repeat until all dinosaurs in the player's party are defeated, as he cannot be beaten. The purpose of the fight is to deal as much damage as possible, as doing so would unlock the special Alpha 06 statue pack.

entities.description:
is an extinct of iguanodontid dinosaur. It lived in the Early Cretaceous period of Mongolia. It was herbivorous and bipedal when walking or running, but probably became quadrupedal when feeding from the ground.

Altirhinus is no. 080 of the Herbivore Ones that can be created in Jurassic Park III: Park Builder.

entities.name: Altispinax
entities.description:
(meaning "with high spines") is a genus of carcharodontosaur theropod dinosaur that lived in England during the Early Cretaceous period known to have caused much confusion among scientists. It was discovered way back in 1884 and has had several names since then. Unfortunately, very little of this dinosaur has been found, which only helps make things confusing. One thing that is known is that it had fairly tall spines on its back, which may have made it look like the North American dinosaur Acrocanthosaurus. However, it is not thought that they were actually related.

An interesting story associated with this dinosaur, although it can't be proven, is that Sir Richard Owen had the tall neural spines of this dinosaur when he was providing direction to Waterhouse Hawkins on how to design his sculptures. The famous Crystal Palace dinosaur sculptures, which still stand today in London, include what is known as the "Humpbacked Megalosaurus". This humped feature may be a result of Owen's interpretation that these neural spines belonged to Megalosaurus, as was believed in an early assignment of the specimen.

Altispinax appeared in the website Jurassic Park Institute on Dinopedia as Becklespinax.

Altispinax appears in Jurassic World: Chaos Theory under its junior synonym Becklespinax.

entities.name: Alxasaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Alxa lizard") is an extinct genus of therizinosaur theropod dinosaur that lived in Inner Mongolia during the Early Cretaceous period. It is the most complete theropod ever found in Asia. It was one of the first of a group of dinosaurs known as therizinosaurs, which are known for having really long claws on their hands. It had a small head for a meat-eating dinosaur, and although it lived in the last part of the Mesozoic Era, it had some features similar to much earlier dinosaurs.

Alxasaurus is considered by some scientists to be a transitional species from the more traditional looking theropods to the therizinosaurs that were common in Asia during the Cretaceous. It had a shortened tail, long neck, and small skull, resembling in many ways the look of the much earlier prosauropods. Several prominent scientists have suggested that Alxasaurus is the most complete specimen of what was once referred to as segnosaurs.

Alxasaurus was featured on the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Alxasaurus was going to be in the game. However the game was shut down before it could be added.

entities.name: Amargasaurus
entities.description:
("La Amarga lizard") is a genus of dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Argentina and measuring up to 10 meters (33 feet) long. A distinctive feature of this dinosaur are the a pair of parallel rows of tall spines down its neck and back, taller than in any other known sauropod. It is an example of Convergent Evolution; with thyreophoran-like, almost spinosaurian dorsal, cervical, and caudal vertebral spines.

In 2022, recent analyses have shown that Amargasaurus is unlikely to have had sails in life, due to it restricting its neck movement.

Amargasaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Amargasaurus appears in concept art for the 2015 Jurassic Park arcade game but does not appear in the final game itself.

entities.name: American Herring Gull
entities.description:
The (Larus smithsonianus) is a large found in North America.

Adults are white with gray back and wings, black wingtips with white spots, and pink legs. Immature birds are gray-brown and are darker and more uniform than European herring gulls, with a darker tail. As is common with other gulls, they are colloquially referred to simply as seagulls.

A pair of American herring gulls flew near a great white shark that caught a sea lion just before they both get swallowed by the Mosasaurus.

When Ben and Darius were lead out by Sammy, Bumpy the Ankylosaurus is seen playfully chasing three American herring gulls.

entities.name: Ammosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of prosauropod dinosaur from the Early Jurassic in the United States that might be a synonym of Anchisaurus. It was not a very known dinosaur.

Ammosaurus is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia of the Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. However, it would receive a profile in the website Dinosaur Earth on Dinopedia.

It is shown building a nest with its feet, a reference to its name, which means "Sand Lizard".

entities.name: Ampelosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of titanosaurian [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in France, during the Late Cretaceous period. In 2021, fossil analysis revealed that Ampelosaurus is more related to the titanosaurs and may have had signature spikes on its shoulders.

Ampelosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. Its image show a mother and its child.

Ampelosaurus is featured in the game during the release of the Jurassic World: Dominion toyline.

Ampelosaurus is mentioned in the database entry as one of the dinosaurs that coexisted with Pyroraptor.

entities.name: Amphicoelias
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in Colorado, United States during the Late Jurassic period. It has been known to be the largest dinosaur ever (before the discovery of large titanosaurs such as Patagotitan) by a single piece of vertebrae that has been discovered by paleontologist Edward Drinker Cope. However the specific species of Amphicoelias that has these gigantic size estimates, A. fragillimus has been reclassified to , and only the smaller 15 metric ton A. altus is the only remaining valid species of this genus.

Amphicoelias was illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. However, it would receive a dino card in the website Dinosaur Earth on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Amtosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia. It lived in either a desert habitat or swamp habitat alongside Deinocheirus, Maleevus, Gobihadros, Achillobator, Graciliceratops, Erlikosaurus, and Segnosaurus. It also resembled its cousin so much that the species has been assigned to Amtosaurus at first.

Amtosaurus is mentioned in the database entry for the Baynshire Formation, the dig site for Deinocheirus in the game.

Amtosaurus is mentioned again in the database entry for the Baynshire Formation, the dig site for Deinocheirus.

entities.name: Amurosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Amur lizard") is a genus of lambeosaurine [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/hadrosaurid hadrosaurid] dinosaur found in the late Cretaceous period of eastern Asia. Like most lambeosaurs, it would have been a primarily bipedal herbivore with a "duckbill" shaped snout and a hollow crest on top of its head, although such a crest has not been found. Fossil bones of adults are rare, but an adult would most likely have been at least 6 meters (20 feet) long. According to Gregory S. Paul, it was about 8 meters (26 feet) long and weighed about 3,000 kilograms (6,600 lbs).

Its remains were found in the Amur Region in the Asian portion of Russia. This duck-billed dinosaur is the best-known dinosaur in Russia. It is known for a large number of specimens, most of them juveniles, that accumulated on the banks of a river.

Amurosaurus is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia of the Jurassic Park Institute as a flipped and colored Barsboldia. However, it hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

Amber samples of Amurosaurus DNA along with many other animals can be seen in the Hammond Creation Lab in Jurassic World: The Exhibition.

entities.name: Amygdalodon
entities.description:
(meaning "almond tooth") is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Middle Jurassic period. It is one of the few Jurassic dinosaurs from South America. Very little information is known about it and the geological formation it was discovered.

It was one of the earlier South American long-necked dinosaurs, and it lived many millions of years before the huge titanosaurs evolved. Since most of the fossils of the very first dinosaurs came from South America, it is possible that Amygdalodon's ancestors were the early prosauropods from that area.

Amygdalodon is classified as belonging to the same family as Cetiosaurus based on its teeth and some other skeletal similarities. Known from only a few bones and teeth, there is much still to be discovered about this genus.

Amygdalodon was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown attacking an unknown theropod. However, the only known animal from the Cerro Carnerero Formation aside from Amygdalodon is an arthropod.

entities.name: Anasazisaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of hadrosaur dinosaur that lived in New Mexico during the Late Cretaceous period. Only a partial skull has been found to date. The dinosaur was originally believed to be a specimen of Kritosaurus, but later turned out to be a new species during 1993, the year where Jurassic Park was released. It was found in the Kirtland Formation. The hadrosaur has predators like Bistahieversor and Saurornitholestes. Other herbivores that coexist with Anasazisaurus include Kritosaurus, Naashoibitosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Pentaceratops, and Stegoceras.

Anasazisaurus is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. Its image can be found within the files, which may indicate that it would almost receive one. However, it would receive a profile in the website Dinosaur Earth on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Anchiceratops
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of chasmosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in Alberta, Canada during the Late Cretaceous period around 72-71 million years ago. It was very similar in looks to its more famous cousin Triceratops, except that its frill was not solid and it was squarer shaped. Anchiceratops also had shorter horns and was a little smaller than Triceratops.

Barnum Brown of the American Museum of Natural History first discovered Anchiceratops along the Red River in Alberta, Canada in 1912. This original specimen consisted of only the back part of the skull, but since that time a number of specimens have been found, including a nearly complete skeleton now at the National Museum of Canada. Anchiceratops body was very much like other ceratopsians except that it had a very short tail. Its most distinctive feature was its strange neck frill - moderately long and rectangular with small oval openings. On the back of the frill there were six large bony knobs that expanded into short, triangular, backward pointing spikes. Anchiceratops also had two short spikes that curve up and outward. It had a short nasal horn, a very long nose, and two moderate-sized brow horns. It was probably a fairly common dinosaur in its time, as a number of fossils have been found.

Anchiceratops was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown walking in what appear to be a floodplain.

entities.name: Anchiornis
entities.description:
(meaning "near bird") is an extinct genus of paravian theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Jurassic period around 160 million years ago. Like the Microraptor, it has four feathered wings. It also had a greyish body color with red head feather crests and white wings with black tips. Its face was mottled with reddish and black spots.

Darius Bowman mentioned Anchiornis as the possible new dinosaur that Jurassic World had announced while visiting his father Fredrick in a hospital.

While trying to figure out what a mysterious feathered dinosaur could be, Ben Pincus and Gia speculate that it could be a Yutyrannus, a Sinornithosaurus, or an Anchiornis, none of which are known to have been created by anyone as of yet.

Anchiornis is mentioned in the database entry for the Tiaojishan Formation: the dig site for Jeholopterus.

entities.name: Anchisaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of prosauropod sauropodomorph dinosaur that lived in Connecticut during the Early Jurassic period. A small slender quadrupedal herbivore, it could have reared up on its hind legs in some circumstances.

Anchisaurus doesn't appear in the movies or the novels.

Anchisaurus is mentioned in the bad end credits to the SEGA Game Gear and Master System versions of Jurassic Park, listed as Anchisaur in Special Thanks (replacing Hase) alongside Quetzalcoatlus, Hererrasaur, Gallimimus, and Ornitholestes.

Anchisaurus can be created in Jurassic Park III: Park Builder.

entities.name: Andesaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Andes lizard") is a genus of basal titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur which existed during the middle of the Cretaceous Period in South America. Like most sauropods, belonging to one of the largest animals ever to walk the Earth, it would have had a small head on the end of a long neck and an equally long tail. This giant plant-eater is from the same family (titanosaur) as Argentinosaurus. It weighed as much as 16 big elephants! Unfortunately, not enough of this dinosaur has been found to know exactly how big it was or what it really looked like. The only thing that scientists know for sure is that it was really huge.

The discovery of only partial Andesaurus remains has made it difficult to classify this enormous beast. It lived at about the same time as Argentinosaurus, but there appears to be enough differentiation to warrant the establishment of its own genus.

Andesaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown standing on a rock in what appear to be a coastline alongside three turtles in another rock behind it.

entities.name: Animantarx
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of nodosaurid ankylosaurian dinosaur that lived in modern-day western North America during the Late Cretaceous period. Its name translates to "living citadel" in Latin, as a reference to a comment from paleontologist R. S. Lull where he described the ankylosaurs as animated citadels. Only one specimen of Animantarx has been recovered.

Animantarx was added to the game as an epic cunning + resilient dinosaur in Update 3.9.

Animantarx was released in the game as a tournament creature on August 28, 2026.

Animantarx is mentioned in the Jurassic World Dinosaur Field Guide in the entry of Ankylosaurus. It is stated that Animantarx was named in 1998, when it was actually named in 1999.

entities.name: Ankylosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankylosauria ankylosaur] dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous period. It was built like a living tank, with extremely thick, bony plates of armor on its body, even including armored eyelids. Its tail also had a second function; it could act as a deadly club. The club was used to swing around and smash into an attacking dinosaur. Its club was so daunting that not even a Tyrannosaurus rex would want to mess with this alarming species.

As a defensive creature, Ankylosaurus was one of nature's most perfect designs. It was almost impervious to being bitten from above and its long, strong tail muscles would have been able to swing its club with great force, however, the tail wasn't too flexible and could only swing 45 degrees in each direction.

There is very little fossil material from this dinosaur - it was apparently the last and largest of the family of armored dinosaurs. It walked fairly upright on all four legs, carrying its tail off the ground and it is theorized that it would drop to the ground when attacked to use its armor as a shield to cover its legs and underbelly.

It is known that Ankylosaurus lived in known North American Cretaceous locations like the Hell Creek and Lance Formations of the United States and the Canadian Scollard Formation.

entities.name: Antarctopelta
entities.description:
was a genus of ankylosaurian dinosaur with one known species, A. oliveroi, which lived in Antarctica during the Late Cretaceous Period. It was a medium-sized ankylosaur, reaching over 4 meters (13 feet) in length. The single known fossil specimen was discovered on James Ross Island in 1986, constituting the first dinosaur remains ever discovered on Antarctica, although it is the second dinosaur from the continent to be formally named. Like other ankylosaurs, Antarctopelta oliveroi was a stocky, herbivorous quadruped protected by armor plates embedded in the skin.

Although a complete skeleton has not been found, the species is estimated to have reached a maximum length of 6 meters (20 feet) from snout to tail tip. Very little of the skull is known, but all of the known skull fragments were heavily ossified for protection. One bone in particular, identified as a supraorbital, included a short spike which would have projected outwards over the eye. The leaf-shaped teeth are asymmetrical, with the majority of the denticles on the edge closest to the tip of the snout. These teeth are also proportionately large compared to those of other ankylosaurs, with the largest measuring 10 millimeters (0.4 inches) across. This compares to the much larger North American Euoplocephalus, 6–7 meters (20-23 feet) in body length, which had teeth averaging only 7.5 millimeters (0.3 inches) across.

Antarctopelta is unlocked by winning an Antarctopelta card pack in special battle events. Once unlocked, additional individuals can be purchased in the market for 7,000 DNA. No hybrids are associated with this creature.

entities.name: Antarctosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of titanosaurian [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous period. Its name doesn't mean it was found on the frozen continent Antarctica, but rather being found in the south.

Antarctosaurus is one of the largest of the South American long-necked dinosaurs. Some of the fossil bones of this dinosaur led scientists to believe that it could have grown as big as 130 feet (40 m) long! This family also includes Argentinosaurus, another South American giant.

Placing Antarctosaurus into the titanosaur family has come into question based on some recent studies. A specimen nearly twice the size of the type specimen was originally assigned a separate species but is now considered a very large individual of the same species.

Antarctosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Antrodemus
entities.description:
is a dubious genus of allosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic period in what is now Colorado, the United States. It was first described as a species of Poekilopleuron before being renamed in 1873. Many Allosaurus fossils from the Morrison Formation were once attributed to Antrodemus.

Antrodemus was illustrated by Timothy Bradley for the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. Its image can be found within the files, which may indicate that it would almost receive one. The image depicts an individual taking down what appears to be a juvenile Camarasaurus.

entities.name: Anzu
entities.description:
is a genus of oviraptorosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of North and South Dakota. Its fossils were found in the Hell Creek formation. Because of the creature's appearance, it is jokingly nicknamed the "chicken from hell". Anzu is known for being the first well-preserved example of an oviraptorosaur in North America.

Anzu's only appearance in the Jurassic Park franchise is being featured in the Jurassic World: Dinosaur Field Guide, replacing Chirostenotes from the Jurassic Park: Dinosaur Field Guide. This may be because the fossils attributed to Anzu were once referred to Chirostenotes.

entities.name: Apatosaurus
entities.description:
is one of the most famous of the giant Jurassic plant-eaters. It was a sauropod: a member of a race of huge long-necked dinosaurs. It was longer than two school buses and weighed as much as four adult male African elephants. For years, an Apatosaurus body stood with the head of a Camarasaurus on the end of its neck. This was named Brontosaurus and was one of the most popular dinosaurs for many years. In 2015, the Brontosaurus genus was revived and several species of Apatosaurus were resigned to the Brontosaurus genus.

Apatosaurus is a fairly typical member of the diplodocid family - long neck, pillar-like legs, long tapering tail and enormous size. It had, like the other family members, peg-like teeth in a head that seemed very small for such a large creature. Compared to Diplodocus, Apatosaurus has a shorter, thicker neck, and a larger, heavier body. There is much speculation about how much these creatures needed to eat and how such a small head could ingest enough food to fuel such a large body. Some scientists have stated that these huge, small-headed creatures would have needed to eat every waking moment in order to provide enough food to keep such a large body alive. Apatosaurus seemed to have every adaptation needed for continuous eating. Despite looking defenseless other than its huge size, the tail was like a giant bullwhip could probably make a loud cracking sound about 200 decibels, enough to scare or even deafen theropods such as Allosaurus.

In order to facilitate the processing of food, which it could not chew with its teeth. Apatosaurus probably swallowed stones that it kept in a gizzard similar to that found in a chicken. The tough plant fibers would spend time in the gizzard stewing and grinded up by the stones.

The Apatosaurus reaches its full size in 10 years.

entities.name: Appalachiosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Appalachian lizard") is a genus of tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of eastern North America. Like almost all theropods, it was a bipedal predator. Only a juvenile skeleton has been found, representing an animal over 7 meters (23 feet) long and weighing over 600 kilograms (1300 lb), which indicates an adult would have been even larger. It is the most completely known theropod from the eastern part of North America.

Fossils of Appalachiosaurus were found in central Alabama, from the Demopolis Chalk Formation. This formation dates to the middle of the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, or around 77 million years ago. Fossil material assigned to A. montgomeriensis is also known from the Donoho Creek and Tar Heel-Coachman formations of North and South Carolina.

Appalachiosaurus is mentioned in the Level 4 Evo trivia for Deinosuchus.

entities.name: Aquilops
entities.description:
Aquilops is first seen in Jurassic World: Rebirth. Being one of the smaller herbivores in the franchise, it very much resembles its close relative, Microceratus. However, Aquilops possesses a different color scheme, being orange with black stripes, and also has two horns; a nasal horn and a horn on the front of its beak. While no other Aquilops are seen in the franchise aside from Dolores, in Jurassic World: The Game, the Aquilops possess individual color schemes like jade-green with three different shades and they possess quills in back of their tails, these individuals are male[Citation needed].

Dolores, seen with a plant in her mouth, was seen standing on her hind legs, intently watching a young human girl. Her curious demeanor shifted to fright when the girl's older sister scared her away. However, the dinosaur soon returned, making snorting sounds as it cautiously approached the younger girl once more, eventually finding comfort and sleeping on her back.

Aquilops was cloned at a secret research facility on Ile Saint-Hubert by InGen, sometime prior to the island's evacuation in 2010 caused by the Distortus Rex, though the reason for this species was abandoned are unknown. Psittacosaurus was mentioned as possibly being added in the genetic components of Aquilops during their hybridization program, for more genetic diversity.

In 2027, Isabella Delgado, who was shipwrecked on the island alongside her family, was searching for a stick to help brush aside plants, when an Aquilops darts out of a fern bush, and watches her as it eats. Isabella's older sister, Teresa, frightens off the ceratopsian, causing it to run back into the jungle. That night, the Aquilops returned, and while her dad and sister were sleeping, and Xavier was by the river, she feeds it some candy. After starting to trust her more, the dinosaur soon falls asleep on her bag.

entities.name: Aragosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in Spain during the Early Cretaceous period. Scientists have uncovered just enough of Aragosaurus to figure out that it was a large plant-eater similar to Camarasaurus. It would have had a rather large, square skull and a fairly short neck for a sauropod.

Study of Aragosaurus fossils indicate that it is almost identical in many ways to, Camarasaurus, its North American cousin. The evidence gleaned from these fossils indicates that it may have been slightly more gracile.

Aragosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Aralosaurus was found in the Bostobe Formation alongside and many unnamed dinosaurs. It also has its own clade: the Aralosaurini.

Aralosaurus is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. Its image can be found within the files, which may indicate that it would almost get one. However, it would receive a profile in the website Dinosaur Earth on Dinopedia.

It appears to have been bipedal and quite small (about 1 meter long) with a comparatively large head. Unlike many later ceratopsians it had no horns, possessing only a small bony frill projecting from the back of its head.

entities.name: Archaeopteryx
entities.description:
is considered by many to be the link between dinosaurs and birds. It had teeth and claws, but it also had feathers and wings. Archaeopteryx was first discovered in 1860 in Bavarian lithographic limestone quarries. Since that time, only five other specimens have been uncovered, with the best specimens being at the Humboldt Museum in Berlin, Germany and the British Museum.

Archaeopteryx is widely thought of as the first bird. It looked very similar to some modern birds, and several of the specimens clearly show what appear to be true feathers.

Upon closer examination, however, scientists have found some striking differences between Archeopteryx and modern birds. Archaeopteryx had a long, stiff, bony tail, unlike modern birds. Each wing had two separate fingers on the leading wing edges that were equipped with sharp, curved claws which was used to climb up into the tops of trees. The biggest differences, however, are in the skull. It didn't have a beak, but rather a true set of jaws that were equipped with many small, sharp teeth. Internally, there were also many differences in the structure of the hip bones, and Archaeopteryx didn't have a breastbone.

Scientists believe that Archaeopteryx was probably a weak flier. Its skeleton is also uncannily similar to Compsognathus, a small dinosaur that was the size of a pigeon that has been found in the same quarries.

entities.name: Archaeornithomimus
entities.description:
is a genus of theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of China, 70 million years ago. It is related to the more famous Gallimimus, Struthiomimus, and Ornithomimus, lived in the same manner, possibly living in flocks, eating everything from small mammals, to plants and fruit, eggs, to insects, and even hatchlings of other Asian dinosaurs. However, they were also the potential prey for the larger , such as Tarbosaurus.

In the movie, Claire mentions on why Jurassic World picked the name Indominus rex and how hard it is to say this dinosaur's name, while Owen Grady makes a joke with this theropod's name.

entities.name: Argentinosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of herbivorous [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/sauropod sauropod] dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous period. It may have been the largest dinosaur ever, aside from Patagotitan and Bruhathkayosaurus. Like other megasauropods, such as Supersaurus, comparatively little fossils of Argentinosaurus have been found.

Argentinosaurus was discovered by a retired oil worker and was formally described in 1993. The few bones include hipbones, backbones, and a tibia (lower leg bone). One vertebra was over four feet (1.3 m) tall and the tibia was 58 inches (155 cm) long. A number of prominent scientists have stated that this member of the South American titanosaur family was the largest dinosaur that ever lived.

Argentinosaurus appeared in the website Jurassic Park Institute on the Dinopedia section. It was also mentioned in the Jurassic World Dinosaur Field Guide.

Argentinosaurus is unlocked by completing Battle Stage 4. Additional individuals can be purchased in the market for 160 DNA or found in card packs. A level 40 Argentinosaurus can be fused with a level 40 Labyrinthodontia to make the hybrid Labyrinthosaurus.

entities.name: Argyrosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "silver lizard") is an extinct genus of titanosaurian [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous period around 70 million years ago. It might have been the biggest dinosaur ever, but not enough fossil bone has yet been found to know for sure.

It was among the last of the giant titanosaurs, dying out in the great extinction at the end of the Cretaceous. Argyrosaurus' upper leg bone was over 6 feet (2 m) long! Unfortunately, not much more of this dinosaur has been found.

First described in 1893, Argyrosaurus was unquestionably a huge titanosaur. Although other material has been found that may belong to this genus, no definitive association has yet been made.

Argyrosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Arkansaurus
entities.description:
("Arkansas lizard") is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur that was discovered in Lockesburg, Arkansas (USA), living during the Early Cretaceous. Only one species is known: A. fridayi. Its nearest relative is , who also happens to live in the United States. It is named for the state it was found as well as its discoverer J.B. Friday, who found the dinosaur's fossilized foot on his farm in 1972. Arkansaurus was declared the official state dinosaur of Arkansas in 2017. Interestingly, the scientific name was coined in 1977, but would be officially described in 2018. In the meantime, it was declared a nomen dubium.

Arkansaurus fossils come from the Trinity Group, which was home to other dinosaurs such as Acrocanthosaurus - the apex predator of the region - and the giant sauropod Sauroposeidon.

Arkansaurus was illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, depicted for some reason as a carcharodontosaurid rather than an ornithomimid. Nevertheless, it hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

entities.name: Arrhinoceratops
entities.description:
(meaning "no nose-horn face") is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in Canada during the Late Cretaceous period. Another member of the family of frilled and horned dinosaurs that includes Triceratops, this lesser known relative is best recognized by its very short nose horn. Its name literally means no nose horn. It was fairly large, with medium-sized brow horns, and was most likely a typical herd-dwelling plant-eater.

Arrhinoceratops is known from only one skull found along the Red Deer River in 1923. Arrhinoceratops had a short, deep face with large nostrils. It had two moderately long, sharp brow horns that curved forward, with a short, blunt nasal horn. The neck frill was broad and rounded with two small oval fenestrae (openings). Arrhinoceratops was closely related to Triceratops.

Arrhinoceratops was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown walking out of the water onto a coastline while a turtle begins to crawl towards the water.

entities.name: Astrodon
entities.description:
(meaning "star tooth") is an extinct genus of herbivorous [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/sauropod sauropod] dinosaur that lived in eastern United States during the Early Cretaceous period. It was a member of the same family that included the giant Argentinosaurus and the small Magyarosaurus. It was only as big as one school bus! It was also among the first dinosaurs discovered in the U.S., way back in 1886. While most dinosaurs back then were found in the West, Pleurocoelus was uncovered on Maryland's East Coast.

Apart from its small size, Astrodon seems to have been a typical sauropod. Few sauropods, however, have generated so much disagreement among scientists. Specimens originally thought to belong to this genus have variously been ascribed to Camarasaurus and Diplodocus.

Additionally, there is a famous trackway in Texas that is believed to show an Astrodon being stalked by an Acrocanthosaurus. Astrodon used to be the Texas State Dinosaur based on the trackway, but lost its place to the giant Sauroposeidon.

Astrodon was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia, although listed under its synonym Pleurocoelus.

entities.name: Atlasaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Atlas lizard") is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North Africa during the Middle Jurassic period. Since it was discovered very recently, scientists still know very little about its life. Since this dinosaur was only about half the size of Brachiosaurus, it is thought that the African environment could not have supported the giant dinosaurs seen in other parts of the world. However, scientists think that Atlasaurus may have eventually grown as large as the latter because it is believed that sauropods may have continued to grow throughout their lives.

Compared to Brachiosaurus, Atlasaurus had a larger skull, longer tail and somewhat shorter neck. It fits an important niche in the sauropod family lineage and further study of this fairly complete specimen should provide interesting results.

Atlasaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Atlascopcosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Atlas Copco lizard”) is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur that lived in Australia during the Early Cretaceous period. It is known only from a jaw fragment and a few teeth.

It is a good example of how scientists can learn a great deal about a dinosaur from a very small amount of fossil material. Atlascopcosaurus teeth are similar enough to other members of the elasmarian family to place it in that group, but different enough to establish a new genus.

The distinction that leads scientists to believe that it was a separate genus is the number of ridges on the teeth and their placement in the jaw.

Atlascopcosaurus was named for a sponsor of the expedition that discovered the dinosaur - the Atlas Copco Corporation.

entities.name: Atrociraptor
entities.description:
226.7 kilograms (500 pounds) [Jurassic media]

is an extinct genus of dromaeosaur theropod dinosaur that lived in Alberta, Canada during the Late Cretaceous period. It lived in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, living alongside famous species such as the Albertosaurus, Edmontonia, Edmontosaurus, Ornithomimus, Pachyrhinosaurus, and Struthiomimus.

One feature that defines this dromaeosaur from other genera is its somewhat short and tall skull with teeth featuring large serrations giving it the look of a bulky-snouted animal, in which it is hypothesized that Atrociraptor may have had a stronger bite force than other dromaeosaurs or had specialized teeth to bite differently compared to its kin.

Like many of the dinosaurs featured in the Jurassic franchise, the size of the Atrociraptor clones is larger than its real-life counterpart. Roughly the same size as Velociraptors such as Blue, the Atrociraptors stand around 2 meters tall, measure nearly 4 meters long, and weigh around 500 pounds. They have a boxy, stout head build with quills underneath the tip of their lower jaws and a less slender body build compared to Velociraptors and blunt edged sickle claws. One particular pack (trained by Soyona Santos to hunt down anything or anyone marked with a red laser and persistent enough to follow them long distances, and trained with a whistle by The Handler to give them a signal to attacking the targets in order) consisted of four individuals named Ghost, Tiger, Panthera and Red. This pack's coloration varies wildly between individuals - similar to TLW male Velociraptor variant, Panthera and Tiger having orange coloring and black stripes (Tiger is darker in color and with more noticeable stripes), Red with light brown coloring and reddish-orange banding, and Ghost with white coloring with stripes, similar to the JPIII female Velociraptor variant. While Ghost had blood-red eyes, the other three had yellow eyes. The Atrociraptors are also very fast, quick, and agile - they can run between 60 and 100 mph (96.56 to 160.93 k/h), are able to move through and around just about any obstacle, jump great heights and distances, and adapted to changing areas in pursuit of their target.

entities.name: Aublysodon
entities.description:
is a dubious genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in Montana during the Late Cretaceous period. Aublysodon is considered a nomen dubium due to the holotype material referred to the genus was lost, although similar teeth have been recovered from Canada, USA and Asia. This dinosaur is classified in "Aublysodontinae", which consists of Tyrannosauroids that are size morphs, ontogenetic, or identical to already-known, valid genera. One species has remained in the name, A. mirandus, although many have been assigned to Aublysodon, then reassigned.

Aublysodon was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Aurornis
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of anchiornithid theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Jurassic period alongside Anchiornis and Xiaotingia. It was once classified as a troodontid before being put in the anchiornithid family in 2017.

A study from 2017 suggested that Aurornis may be a junior synonym of Anchiornis, as the two dinosaurs lived in the same area.

Aurornis is mentioned in the database entry for the Tiaojishan Formation, the dig site for Jeholopterus.

entities.description:

entities.name: Australovenator
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of megaraptoran theropod dinosaur that lived in Australia during the Late Cretaceous Period. During the 1900s, it was considered to be an alvarezsaurid or an intermediate theropod. During the 1990s, the dinosaur is believed to be a member of the allosaur family. It was then referred to as the "Polar Allosaur", which also appeared in the famous dinosaur documentary "Walking With Dinosaurs". As of 2009, the theropod was discovered to be a megaraptorid and was named Australovenator. It is considered to be a sister taxon to Fukuiraptor.

Australovenator is possibly illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia of the Jurassic Park Institute as a flipped and colored Compsosuchus. However, it hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

Aside from that, it is mentioned in the description of Fukuiraptor, being referred to as the Australian species of Allosaurus.

In the Jurassic Park III: Park Builder, you can uncover an Allosaurus in Australia. Given that no animal with the name Allosaurus is currently believed to have existed in Australia it is likely that this creature is based off of Australovenator fossils which were once simply classified as "Allosaurus robustus".
