entities.name: Austroraptor
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of paravian theropod dinosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Argentina. It is commonly considered to be a Dromaeosaurid, but some studies place it in the proposed family Unenlagiidae.

Austroraptor was a large, moderately-built, ground-dwelling, bipedal carnivore, estimated at 5-6 meters (16-20 feet) long. It is one of the largest dromaeosaurids known, with only Achillobator, Dakotaraptor, and Utahraptor approaching or surpassing it in length.

It is theorized that Austroraptor and its relatives preyed on fish due to the shape of their teeth.

Austroraptor was found within the game's audio files of Jurassic World Evolution 2. Being cut from the game, eventually, this species made it in the sequel, Jurassic World Evolution 3 in the Wetlands Pack.

entities.name: Austrosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Southern lizard") is an extinct genus of titanosaur sauropod dinosaur that lived Queensland, Australia during the Early Cretaceous period. Although the large sauropod fossil is made up of only a few broken bones, scientists have determined that it may fit into the same family as brachiosaurids. However, it was later found to be part of the titanosaurs.

This was only the second sauropod to be discovered in Australia and there are very few remains. A few partial bones of a larger sauropod from another Australian site may belong to this genus.

Austrosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Avaceratops
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in northwest of the United States during the Late Cretaceous period. Like many dinosaur discoveries, not much of it was found. In fact, scientists only found part of its skull and a little of the skeleton behind its head.

This small ceratopsian is known from a single partial skeleton. It was small but had a moderately heavy build. Avaceratops had a short, deep snout with a thick and powerful lower jaw. The neck frill was solid. It is believed that this ceratopsian did not have very large brow horns. Most of its closest relatives had a large nose horn and no brow horns. Some feel that the type specimen is a juvenile, or possibly a young adult. It is considered a primitive ceratopsian.

It was found in 1981 by two amateur paleontologists, Ed and Ava Cole and it was named after Ava. It is an example of the important contributions that non-scientists can make to paleontology. This skeleton is now on display at the Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia.

Avaceratops was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. It is outdated, being depicted with one horn instead of two.

entities.description:
Return to Jurassic Park VI}} was a of theropod dinosaur that lived in the late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia, around 70 million years ago. Avimimus was a small dinosaur with a length of 1.5 meters (5 feet). The skull was small compared to the body, though the brain and eyes were large.

Avimimus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Avimimus is no. 022 of the Carnivore Ones that can be created in Jurassic Park III: Park Builder.

A group of Avimimus that were genetically modified to possess plumage were created by Dr. Gustavus in a hidden lab in Jurassic Park. These animals were later discovered by InGen scientists Derrick Hoyle and Abby Nakajima, who had snuck into Gustavus' lab in order to find out what he was working on. Gustavus soon returned to his lab and, upon discovering the two, introduced them to some of his creations, including the Avimimus, before attempting to kill them.

(meaning "bird lizard") is an extinct genus of enantiornithine bird from the Late Cretaceous of North America.

It is known to have lived in the Hell Creek Formation, where it is inhabited by Tyrannosaurus rex, Triceratops, Pachycephalosaurus, Struthiomimus, and Ankylosaurus.

entities.name: Bactrosaurus
entities.description:
is a genus of herbivorous dinosaur that lived in China during the late Cretaceous around 70 million years ago. Bactrosaurus is one of the earliest known hadrosaurid. It was a very early ancestor of Lambeosaurus, another duckbill. Like its relatives, Bactrosaurus was a plant-eater that had many hundreds of teeth, long back legs and short front legs, and a beak on the front of its mouth for cutting and tearing tough plants.

Bactrosaurus was more powerfully built than most other hadrosaurs and was very heavy for its size. It almost appears to be a transitional animal linking iguanodonts with hadrosaurs, and researchers have noted that it almost looks more like an iguanodont than a hadrosaur.

Bactrosaurus is mentioned in the entry of Archaeornithomimus and Gigantoraptor.

Bactrosaurus is mentioned in the database entry for Archaeornithomimus.

entities.name: Bagaceratops
entities.description:
(meaning "small horned face") is an extinct genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period around 72 to 71 million years ago. It was a very small member of the ceratopsian (horn faced) family of dinosaurs. It looked very much like its better-known relative, Protoceratops, except for the head. Unlike its cousin, Bagaceratops head was shaped almost like a perfect triangle and it had a very small frill.

This basal member of the ceratopsian family had no brow horns, but it did have a well-developed beak with cheek teeth that were perfectly suited for grinding coarse plants. Scientists have collected five complete skulls and almost 20 partial skulls, as well as many skeletal bones. These fossils represent different stages of growth, so scientists have a fairly complete understanding of Bagaceratops life cycle.

An interesting fact is that, although Bagaceratops came along millions of years later than Protoceratops, Bagaceratops is considered a more primitive creature.

Bagaceratops was featured in Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. Its artwork shows a colored male alongside a resting female.

entities.name: Bahariasaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Bahariya lizard") is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in North Africa during the Late Cretaceous period around 95 million years ago. Very little is known about Bahariasaurus as only a small number of hipbones have been found. Even those were lost, however, when Allied bombs destroyed the German museum where the bones were housed during WWII.

A number of these bones were found by German paleontologists shortly before WWI. In the early 1930's they were named Bahariasaurus and identified as coming from a huge carnivore. WWI ended the original search for the specimen and WWII destroyed what had been found. Some scientists have suggested that Bahariasaurus may have been part of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/tyrannosaurid Tyrannosauridae] family. However, no Tyrannosauroid has been recorded in Africa. Others believe that Deltadromeus should be a junior synonym of Bahariasaurus.

Bahariasaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Bajadasaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous epoch (late Berriasian to Valanginian stages) of northern Patagonia, Argentina. It was first described in 2019, based on a single specimen found in 2010 that includes a largely complete skull and parts of the neck. The only species is Bajadasaurus pronuspinax. The genus is classified as a member of the Dicraeosauridae, a group of comparatively small and short-necked sauropods that lived from the Early or Middle Jurassic to the end of the Early Cretaceous.

Bajadasaurus appears as a rare resilient dinosaur in the game since Update 1.11.

entities.name: Bambiraptor
entities.description:
("Bambi thief") is an extinct genus of dromeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Montana during the Late Cretaceous period. It is one of the most important fossils found in North America. This little bird-like dinosaur was a very quick hunter, and it may have been an important step in dinosaurs' evolution into birds. Scientists believe that feathers and fuzz covered its body. The fuzz would have been like the downy covering on baby birds. Bambiraptor had quite a few features in common with modern birds. It had a wishbone, something all modern birds have that allow them to flap their wings, and its arms and hands were very long for its body size. In fact, the length of its arms and hands approached the lengths needed for flight. It also had an ossified sternum, a bone that is essential for birds to be able to move their wings for flying.

Even with these similarities, however, there is no doubt that Bambiraptor was still a dinosaur from the raptor family. It had the killer claw on its foot like Velociraptor, and it had a mouth full of sharp teeth. Bambiraptor is considered by many to be the North American version of Archaeopteryx. Clearly a short step away from its European relative, this specimen is an exceptionally important piece of the bird/dinosaur puzzle. With more than 90 percent of the animal discovered, along with the remains of what may be a second individual, this specimen will continue to provide insight into the evolution of birds.

Bambiraptor is named after the character Bambi from the Disney movie of the same name. However, some people claim that "Bambi" is short for the Italian word "Bambino," which means baby.

Bambiraptor was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Barapasaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of basal sauropod dinosaur that lived in India during the Early Jurassic period. Barapasaurus was one of the earliest of the giant, long-necked plant-eaters. It is very well known because many different individuals have been found. The only trouble is, no head has been discovered, so its complete look remains a mystery.

The bone bed where Barapasaurus was discovered contained the remains of as many as 300 sauropod specimens. Consequently, the composite skeleton constructed from these fossils may have some proportional errors.

Barapasaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Barosaurus
entities.description:
was a large sauropod dinosaur from the Diplodocidae family from the late Jurassic period, in what is the United States. It was closely related to Diplodocus.

Known primarily from one partial skeleton described in 1890 (re-described in 1919), and possibly a second species from Africa, Barosaurus is very similar to Diplodocus except for unusually long cervical (neck) vertebrae. The specimen was originally named Gigantosaurus based on its size. Its spectacularly long neck is showcased in a somewhat controversial pose in the rotunda of the American Museum of Natural History. The dinosaur is shown rearing up on its hind legs in a defensive posture with its head more than 30 feet in the air. Some paleontologists have stated that it would have been impossible for this dinosaur to stand like that.

Barosaurus is among the dinosaurs that appeared in the Dinopedia section of the now defunct Jurassic Park Institute.

Though no living animals of this species make an appearance in the film, Barosaurus is mentioned on a sign depicting the map of Gyrosphere Valley.

entities.name: Barsboldia
entities.description:
(meaning "of Barsbold", a well-known Mongolian paleontologist) is an extinct genus of hadrosaur dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. It was named after Rinchen Barsbold, a famous Mongolian paleontologist.

Barsboldia is part of the Saurolophinae subfamily, who were common in Asia during the Cretaceous period. The huge size of this duckbill indicates that the Gobi Desert was once a much different environment with lots of plants and water.

Some scientists proposed that Barsboldia isn't a valid genus and is a synonym to Hypacrosaurus. However, this isn't true nowaday due to the fact that Hypacrosaurus isn't a member of the Saurolophinae subfamily, and dinosaurs from Asia and North America, while being similar to each other, are different species as a whole.

Barsboldia was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. It is inaccurately portrayed with a crest on its head, something that the real dinosaur didn't have.

entities.name: Baryonyx
entities.description:
(meaning "heavy claw") is an extinct genus of , a member and of the same group as and a close relative to the northern African dinosaurs Spinosaurus and Suchomimus. Baryonyx was smaller than these relatives but was still a big predator. It was 10 meters (33 feet) long and 2.5 meters (8.25 feet) tall at the hips. However, studies in the fossils of Baryonyx indicate that it had not yet reached its adult stage, so it could be larger, and another study found that there were vertebrae a little larger than others, which would indicate a possible candle or hump in the adult specimen.

It had a long, narrow snout filled with teeth that were cone-shaped, a real difference from the blade-shaped teeth of typical meat-eating dinosaurs.

Because of the shape of its snout and teeth (both of which are similar to those of modern crocodilians), some paleontologists think that Baryonyx ate lots of fish. Others, however, think it ate other dinosaurs. In fact, both ideas are supported by the original Baryonyx specimen from Surrey, England. In the guts of this dinosaur, paleontologists found the partially digested scales of large fish as well as the partially digested bones of a young Iguanodon. This strongly supports the idea that Baryonyx ate both fish and dinosaurs.

A 2022 study comparing the bone densities of Baryonyx and its close relatives, Spinosaurus and Suchomimus revealed that Baryonyx and Spinosaurus possessed very dense bones and could dive and swim in deep water. By comparison, Suchomimus was more suited to wading after prey in shallow water.

entities.name: Becklespinax
entities.description:
Becklespinax (now scientifically synonymous with Altispinax), is a genus of theropod dinosaur, that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now England.

The Becklespinax clones have an appearance based on recent depictions by paleontologists that resemble Concavenator. Like many of the cloned theropods, they have pronated wrists. The clones also have large white spines sticking out from the back of their necks and a small sail on their back. One of them is colored jaded green with a red face, a yellow neck, and black markings; the other is colored various shades of brown, with splotchy darker markings on its snout.

The Becklespinax was shown to be a formidable hunter that doesn't seem to give up on its prey, as even when one was distracted by a hologram, it refocused a short while after. However, they were willing to give up if they are stuck in a river due to the risk of drowning. The Becklespinax was shown being able to coexist with herbivorous dinosaurs in the same enclosure like Brachiosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Gallimimus, and Stegosaurus without attacking them. Albeit, this is probably due to the watering hole in the center of the enclosure, as both herbivorous and carnivorous dinosaurs have been show to coexist in such areas such as this. Despite this seemingly passive nature, Becklespinax have an aggressive temperament at times, especially towards other predators, as one is shown to attack a T. rex hologram despite believing it to be that actual creature.

These animals are also notable for being able to hold their breath for a surprising amount of time. As one individual was able to survive underwater for a short period of time without oxygen. Possibly hinting at a somewhat semi-aquatic nature.

entities.name: Beelomodon
entities.description:
"" ("Beelem's tooth") is a genus of undescribed theropod, possibly belonging to a coelurosaur, that lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now Wyoming, the United States. It is only known two teeth found, thus rendering the dinosaur informally named. The name appeared in print in 1997, when paleontologist Robert T. Bakker mentioned it in a symposium for the Academy of Natural Sciences. He never gave any breakdown of the prefix "beelem-", rendering its etymological name speculation.

While it is considered today as a nomen dubium, Beelemodon was likely part of the fauna from the Morrison Formation.

Beelemodon was illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute. However, it hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

entities.name: Beipiaosaurus
entities.description:
("Beipiao lizard") is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/therizinosaurid therizinosaurid] theropod dinosaur that lived during the early Cretaceous Period.

Beipiaosaurus is known from one partial skeleton from the Yixian Formation in northeastern China. The volcanic ash that formed the mud of this formation was so fine-grained that it preserved very small details of the animals buried in it.

Fossils show that Beipiaosaurus‘s body was covered with long, slender filaments. These filaments were a sort of protofeather, a body cover that eventually evolved into true feathers in birds and some other dinosaurs (such as Caudipteryx). The protofeathers of Beipiaosaurus might have been used for insulation or for display, or for both.

Beipiaosaurus was featured in some concept art for . However, Colin Trevorrow confirmed there were no plans for it to be added it to the final cut.

entities.name: Bellusaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "beautiful lizard") is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Middle Jurassic period.

This Chinese dinosaur from midway in the Jurassic was an ancestor of truly giant plant-eaters. Like latter and larger four legged herbivores, Bellusaurus was a sauropod. Sauropods had tiny heads and weak teeth. Many relied on stomach stones to help them grind their food.

Bellusaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Bellusaurus is mentioned in the database entry as a prey for Monolophosaurus.

entities.description:
is an extinct genus of abelisaur theropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous in the Netherlands. Living in the Maastricht Formation, it seems that Betasuchus is an opportunist carnivore that hunt hadrosaurs and eat carcass of dead marine reptiles near the coasts. It can swim, but by doing so, it become a prey to Mosasaurus.

Betasuchus is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

The same image seen in the Jurassic Park Institute was also used for art in one of the gift shops in Islands of Adventure.

entities.name: Bistahieversor
entities.description:
(meaning "Bistahi destroyer"), also known as the "Bisti Beast", is a genus of eutyrannosaurian tyrannosauroid theropod dinosaur that lived in New Mexico during the Late Cretaceous period. First described in 1990 as a specimen of Aublysodon, it would receive its name 20 years later. A study paper in 2025 recovered Bistahieversor as a member of the Albertosaurines alongside .

This theropod hails from the Kirtland Formation, which housed ceratopsians like Pentaceratops as well as hadrosaurs like Anasazisaurus, Kritosaurus, Parasaurolophus, and Naashoibitosaurus.

Bistahieversor is among the dinosaurs that you could find in the game.

Bistahieversor has been confirmed to appear in Jurassic World: Dino Trackers. This will be the first time it has ever physically appeared in the Jurassic Park Franchise and as well as a toy.

entities.name: Blikanasaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropodomorpha sauropodomorph] prosauropod dinosaur that lived in South Africa during the Late Triassic period. It was one of the earliest dinosaurs, and one of the first of what would evolve into the big, long-necked [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaurs.

Blikanasaurus was an African dinosaur whose ancestors may have walked to Africa from South America. It was fairly heavy for its size, and as such, it was one of the first dinosaurs to begin walking primarily on four legs - although it probably still could have moved about on two legs.

Blikanasaurus represents a unique point in dinosaur evolution as it seems to demonstrate how nature experiments with different designs. In fact, there is still discussion as to whether Blikanasaurus was an evolutionary dead end as some of its characteristics don't appear in later sauropods. One example is that this animal had a greatly reduced fifth metatarsal (foot bone); this bone was much larger in later sauropods and it is not likely that it would have evolved to become larger.

Blikanasaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Blue-and-yellow Macaw
entities.description:
The (Ara ararauna), also known as the blue-and-gold macaw, is a species of parrot that lives in the jungles, woodlands, and savannahs of South America. It is recognisable by its colors: mostly blue dorsum, light yellow/orange venter, and gradient hues of green on top of its head. It is a popular bird in pet trades. Domesticated blue-and-yellow macaws will "scream" or make other loud noises for attention.

Mark Degler has a pet blue-and-yellow macaw named Jack. He is seen in his cage when Alan Grant is having dinner with Ellie Sattler and Mark Degler. Alan stands by the bird's cage, holding a treat. He questions the macaw to see if it remembers his name, although he receives no response. Ellie laughs, and Grant moves towards the dining table.

entities.name: Bonitasaura
entities.description:
is a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur hailing from uppermost layers of the Late Cretaceous Bajo de la Carpa Formation, Neuquen Group, located in Río Negro Province, Northwestern Patagonia, Argentina. The remains, consisting of a partial sub-adult skeleton jumbled in a small area of fluvial sandstone, including lower jaw with teeth, partial vertebrae series and limb bones, were described by Apesteguía in a short communication in mid-2004.

The genus name Bonitasaura refers to the fossil quarry’s name, "La Bonita", while the name of the type species: B. salgadoi, pays homage to Leonardo Salgado: a renowned Argentine paleontologist.

Bonitasaura is unlocked by completing an Earth Shattering [https://jurassicpark.fandom.com/wiki/Events/JW%3A_TG event]. Once unlocked, additional individuals can be purchased in the market for 150 DNA or found in card packs.

entities.name: Borealopelta
entities.description:
is a genus of nodosaurid ankylosaur dinosaur that lived in Alberta, Canada during the Early Cretaceous period. Its remains were discovered on March 21, 2011, at an oil sands mine that is north of Fort McMurray. The area was a sea at the time. It should be noted that keratin sheaths, overlying skin, and stomach contents were well preserved in the specimen, which is rare among dinosaur fossils.

Also, known as the Suncor nodosaur, Borealopelta would be properly named in 2017. Even though it wasn't a feathered dinosaur, have been found. Thus, the dinosaur has a reddish pinkish skin tone.

Borealopelta's discovery was referenced in the database entry of Nodosaurus.

Borealopelta is present within the Jurassic World: Dino Trackers collection.

entities.name: Borogovia
entities.description:
(meaning "borogoves") is an extinct genus of carnivorous [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/troodontid troodontid] theropod dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. Discovered in 1971 and described in 1987, fossils of this dinosaur were found in the Nemegt Formation, which housed popular known dinosaurs like Tarbosaurus, Nemegtosaurus, and Saichania. It was also considered to be a possible specimen of Saurornithoides by 1982 before being referred to be a new species. The name is derived from the fantasy creatures called "borogoves" in the Lewis Carroll poem "Jabberwocky" in Through the Looking-Glass.

Borogovia was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Borogovia is mentioned in the entry for Sinornithoides.

entities.name: Bothriospondylus
entities.description:
(meaning "excavated vertebra") is an extinct genus of neosauropod [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in England during the Late Jurassic period. It was found in the Kimmeridge Clay and was described by Richard Owen in 1875, basing his description on a few backbones. Like Brachiosaurus, it would have had front legs longer than its back legs and probably held its head high above the ground to feed on the upper branches of trees.

There is no modern scientific description of Bothriospondylus. In the last part of the 20th century, two species of this genus were reassigned to Pelorosaurus. A species found in Madagascar has not been widely accepted as belonging to this genus.

Bothriospondylus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its image, it is shown pushing an unknown theropod.

entities.name: Brachyceratops
entities.description:
(meaning "short horned face") is an extinct genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in Montana, United States during the Late Cretaceous period. Its classification is tenuous at best, as scientists think that the type specimen may in fact be a juvenile animal of another genus, possibly Centrosaurus.

Whatever the case may be, the fact remains that this specimen was a small, plant-eating horned dinosaur that may have been separated from its herd and killed by a predator, such as an Albertosaurus. Like others in its family, it had a long frill of bone at the back of its skull that was probably used to protect its neck from predators and to help attract the opposite sex.

The genus Brachyceratops has no other species and, since it is a juvenile, there is much speculation as to whether it should be regarded as a genus. In the past, this specimen has been variously assigned to Monoclonius and Centrosaurus. More recent study of the specimen seems to show differences between this specimen and Monoclonius, so the debate goes on.

entities.name: Brachylophosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "short-crested lizard") is a mid-sized member of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/hadrosaurid hadrosaurid] family of dinosaurs. It is known from several skeletons and bonebed material from the Judith River Formation of Montana, the Wahweap Formation of Utah and the Oldman Formation of Alberta, living about 81-76.7 million years ago.

It is famous for its dinosaur mummy named "Leonardo", who was discovered in 2000.

entities.name: Brachypodosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "short-footed lizard") is a dubious genus of dinosaur, possibly an ornithischian (more specifically an ankylosaur), from the Late Cretaceous Lameta Formation (Maastrichtian) in India.

The only remains discovered so far for this animal consist of a single fossil bone, excavated at the Chota Simla Hill near Jabalpur. In 1934, geologist Dhirendra Kishore Chakravarti, of the Geological Museum of the Banaras Hindu University, considered it a humerus, of a stegosaurian. He named it as the type species Brachypodosaurus gravis. The generic name is derived from Greek βραχύς: "brachys" ("short"), and πούς: "pous" ("foot"). The specific name "gravis" means "heavy" in Latin. Chakravarti hereby became the first local scientist to name a dinosaur.

The holotype is IM V9. The bone is over a foot long. Chakravarti based his identification of the element as a humerus on the presence of a large crest on the shaft, which he took for the deltopectoral crest. The status as a (dinosaurian) humerus is problematic. The bone is flat, has a crest on the other side of the shaft also, is not twisted around its longitudinal axis, is strongly constricted above and below the crests and lacks a clear "caput" or condyles. In any case, it lacks stegosaurian synapomorphies. On the assumption it might at least be some member of the Thyreophora, it has been considered a possible ankylosaurian, the ankylosaurs being a sister group of the Stegosauria that survived into the Late Cretaceous. Even then, however, it was considered a nomen dubium as so few remains of the animal have been found. In 2004, Matthew Lamanna e.a. considered it unlikely that any Ornithischia were present in the Maastrichtian of India. The other Late Cretaceous genus from India originally described as a stegosaur, Dravidosaurus, is also a nomen dubium based on plesiosaurian remains.

Brachypodosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia as a flipped and recolored Edmontonia.

entities.description:
(meaning "short horned face") is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur closely related to Protoceratops that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous period. Like its relative, it would have browsed the dry Cretaceous land for low-growing plants. It is another example of the development of the ceratopsian family in Asia.

Originally assigned to Protoceratops, there is still discussion as to whether this specimen deserves its own genus. It may eventually be reassigned to Bagaceratops. However, this may not be happening as Bagaceratops lived during the Maastrichtian while Breviceratops comes from the Campanian.

Breviceratops was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Brontosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Jurassic period of North America. It was originally a different genus from Apatosaurus, but the type species Brontosaurus excelsus was reclassified as a species of Apatosaurus called Apatosaurus excelsus, meaning Brontosaurus was considered scientifically invalid for over 110 years. However, an extensive study published in 2015 by a joint research team of United Kingdom and Portugal concluded that Brontosaurus was a valid genus of sauropod distinct from Apatosaurus, resurrecting the genus.

Though no living animals of this species make an appearance in the film, Brontosaurus is briefly mentioned by Tim Murphy, who misidentifies Jurassic Park's Brachiosaurus as Brontosaurus.

Though no living animals of this species make an appearance in the film, Brontosaurus is mentioned on a sign depicting the map of Gyrosphere Valley.

In Season 1, Kenji misidentified a Brachiosaurus as Brontosaurus, with Darius explaining the park does not have this dinosaur.

entities.name: Brown Pelican
entities.description:
The (Pelecanus occidentalis) is a species of pelican and 1 of 3 pelican species found in the Americas. The brown pelican is found on the Atlantic Coast from New Jersey to the mouth of the Amazon River, and along the Pacific Coast from British Columbia to Peru, including the Galapagos Islands.

Alan Grant spotted a flock of brown pelicans flying over the ocean outside the helicopter as it flew away from Isla Nublar, a reminder of birds being the only surviving dinosaurs (like the ones he and the others escaped from).

entities.name: Bruhathkayosaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "huge-bodied lizard") is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/sauropod sauropod] dinosaur that lived in India during the Late Cretaceous period. This giant dinosaur with a really long name could be the biggest dinosaur ever discovered. For several years it was thought to be a gigantic meat-eater, but it was recently classified as a sauropod, the long-necked family of dinosaurs that includes Argentinosaurus. Bruhathkayosaurus was among the largest dinosaurs that ever lived and would have been an awesome sight to see. It was about twice as big as a Tyrannosaurus rex.

Some scientists don't think that the Bruhathkayosaurus fossils clearly illustrate the dinosaur's size. These scientists believe the actual size may have been somewhat smaller, but still very impressive.

Bruhathkayosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Tiny Bryonosaurus skulls were found inside the nest of a Citipati. It was claimed once that the dinosaur does nest parasite, but this has been disproven.

Byronosaurus was illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute. However, it hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

entities.name: Caenagnathasia
entities.description:
(meaning "recent jaw from Asia") is an extinct genus of caenagnathid theropod dinosaur that lived in Uzbekistan during the Late Cretaceous period. This little dinosaur is a member of the family of that includes Oviraptor and Gigantoraptor. Very little fossil evidence has been found of this dinosaur, only parts of a lower jaw. It is a great example of how paleontologists can make educated guesses about how dinosaurs may have actually looked. They don't really know for sure, but they are always searching for more fossil evidence to confirm their theories.

Dr. Philip Currie, an advisor to the Jurassic Park Institute, led the team that discovered Caenagnathasia. Dr. Currie noted that this finding was very important because this specimen is the smallest member of this family ever found. He also said the discovery proves that these dinosaurs evolved several million years earlier than scientists previously thought.

Caenagnathasia was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Caenagnathus
entities.description:
(meaning "recent jaw") is a genus of caenagnathid theropod that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alberta, Canada. It has a confusing history; it was discovered in 1936 based on a set of jaws, which were thought to be those of a bird. By 1988, with the use of a specimen obtained from the storage, Caenagnathus had been synonymized with Chirostenotes. However, this synonymy has been doubted, and it was later found that both oviraptorosaurs were separate species.

Today, Caenagnathus is known from partial remains such as lower jaws, a tail vertebra, and hand bones. Its sister taxon is Anzu.

Caenagnathus is mentioned in the description for Chirostenotes in the Dinosaur Field Guide.

entities.name: Camarasaurus
entities.description:
was a very heavily built member of the long-necked [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] family of Jurassic dinosaurs. It is very well known by scientists and recently a family of these large creatures was discovered in the Western U.S. Camarasaurus is also a part of one of paleontology's big mistakes when it was thought that its head was put on the body of Apatosaurus and called Brontosaurus, although a study in 2015 showed that Brontosaurus was a distinct genus from Apatosaurus.

Compared to some of the other sauropods, Camarasaurus had a relatively short neck and tail. It also had a large head compared to other sauropods, but the head was almost hollow. The skull openings for the nose and eyes were very large. This is the most common North American sauropod found, with more than ten fairly complete skeletons unearthed to date. At least four species have been identified within this genus.

Camarasaurus gets its name from the hollow spaces in its neck vertebrae. These would have made the neck lighter and easier for the dinosaur to lift and move about. This dinosaur also had the largest teeth among sauropods.

Camarasaurus was featured in some concept art for Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom. However, Colin Trevorrow confirmed there were no plans for it to be added to the final cut.

entities.name: Camptosaurus
entities.description:
is an ornithopod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic period.

First discovered in 1877, there have been more than 20 skulls and 12 skeletons found to date of this dinosaur. This leads scientists to think of it as a fairly common plant-eater of the last part of the Jurassic and the first part of the Cretaceous. It belongs to the same family as Iguanodon, although it was an earlier dinosaur.

There is ongoing debate regarding the various specimens currently attributed to the genus Camptosaurus. Some scientists believe that a number of the species should be renamed after the type specimen and that their differences are simply individual variation. There have been a number of dinosaurs that were originally classified as Camptosaurus, including an Allosaurus species.

Camptosaurus doesn't seem to be one of the dinosaurs recreated by InGen, but its name is on the name tag of a Jurassic World employee named James. It is unknown if other employees share this title or if it is exclusive to him, or if Camptosaurus was cloned by Masrani for exhibition at Jurassic World.

entities.name: Canada Goose
entities.description:
The (Branta canadensis) is a species of goose recognizable by its black head and neck, white cheeks and chin, and a brown body. It is native to the arctic and temperate regions of North America, and has been known to migrate to warmer lands during the winter. In fact, the Canada goose is best known for its migration.

During recent years, populations of Canada geese have grown substantially, most likely due to the absence of natural predators alongside an abundance of safe, human-made bodies of water near food sources.

Males display aggressive behavior during breeding and nesting rounds, rarely involving interspecific killing.

A flock of Canada geese is migrating alongside a flock of Pteranodon and three Quetzalcoatlus somewhere in North America after the events of the Biosyn Incident.

entities.name: Carcharodontosaurus
entities.description:
was a genus in the family. It was a large carnivore that lived in Northern Africa in the Late Cretaceous Period, the same time and place as Spinosaurus. Measuring 12.5 meters (41 feet) long and weighing more than six tonnes, it was among the largest predatory dinosaurs. Additionally, it gets its name from its sharp, serrated teeth which resemble the teeth seen in a great white shark, or known by its scientific name "Carcharodon carcharias".

In the game Jurassic Park: Explorer, the following information is given about this creature:

"Native to North Africa, Carcharodontosaurus had an enormous jaw with long serrated teeth that were up to 8 inches long. It's long muscular legs might have allowed it to run at speeds of up to 20 mph/ 32 kmph."

Carcharodontosaurus appeared in the website Jurassic Park Institute on Dinopedia.

(meaning "heart tooth") is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/sauropod sauropod] dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic period in England. It was the first sauropod to be ever named, specifically by Richard Owen in 1841. Being very obscure, it is usually referred to as a species or a potential synonym of Cetiosaurus. However, recent studies show that this dinosaur is a different genus and is possibly related to Turiasaurus.

Cardiodon is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006. The artwork is a flipped and recolored Kotasaurus.

entities.name: Carnotaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "meat-eating bull") is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous period. It was one of the most bizarre yet dangerous meat-eating dinosaurs ever found. Its skull was short, with spiked armor in the form of feature scales across its body (skin impressions show this, although it is unknown around the face since the impressions for that area were destroyed) on the top and a pair of knobby horns over its small eyes. The neck and shoulder blades were well developed, but the arms were incredibly short, with forearms so shrunken they were practically just wrists; not even Tyrannosaurus rex had such small arms. In 2021, it is revealed that Carnotaurus has scaly skin instead of osteoderms.

With its small skull and weak bite force, Carnotaurus might not have been able to attack big plant-eaters, but it was probably fast due to its long and powerfully built legs and could have easily chased down smaller, agile prey. In fact, research has indicated that despite Carnotaurus’ small head, its jaws were able to open very wide apart from other theropod dinosaurs in order to catch prey.

The horns of Carnotaurus look something like those of a bull - and like a bull, it may have used them in contests with others of its own species. In this way, two Carnotaurus could test each other's strength without either of them seriously injuring the other.

There seem to be at least three color variations of the Carnotaurus: one is a subdued red with several black marks across its entire body. This variant of Carnotaurus is the most commonly-seen, and there are at least three individuals known to exist in-canon with this colour scheme. The second variant is mainly black with reddish-pink marks going from the face and across the back nicknamed "Boss" by the Nublar Six in Jurassic World: Chaos Theory. Meanwhile, the third variant possess green body with light brown belly and a light red-orange stripe running from it snout to it back and all the way to the tip of it tail.

entities.name: Cassowary
entities.description:
(Indonesian: kasuari; Biak: man suar 'bird strong'; Tok Pisin: muruk; Papuan: kasu weri 'horned head') are ratites (flightless birds without a keel on their sternum bones) of the genus Casuarius native to the tropical forests of New Guinea, the Moluccas, and northeastern Australia. There are three species of cassowary: the (Casuarius casuarius), the (Casuarius unappendiculatus), and the (Casuarius bennetti),; as well as a fourth extinct species: the (Casuarius lydekkeri). Its closest living relative is the emu.

It is recognizable by its blue head and its keratinous casque, which is used for communications, similar to the hadrosaurs of the Cretaceous period. Its main weapon is their feet, which are equipped with sharp claws. Cassowaries kick their attacker with their powerful legs, proving the claw lethal.

The cassowary has been labeled the world's most dangerous bird, since it is known to attack both people and dogs, though it pales in comparison to the common ostrich, which kills two or three humans per year in South Africa. The bird is usually wary of humans. However, when it is provoked, it is capable of inflicting serious, even fatal, injuries.

DNA of a cassowary was used by for a scraped hybrid in Jurassic World: Camp Cretaceous, along with Rugops and Yutyrannus.

entities.description:
(meaning "tail feather") is a genus of peacock-sized theropod dinosaur that lived in the Aptian age of the early Cretaceous Period (about 124.6 million years ago). They were feathered and remarkably birdlike in their overall appearance, to the point that some paleontologists think it was a bird. Two species have been described: C. zoui (the type species), in 1998, and C. dongi, in 2000.

Caudipteryx fossils were first discovered in the Yixian Formation of the Sihetun area of Liaoning Province, northeastern China in 1997.

Caudipteryx was among the dinosaurs to have appeared in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute.

Caudipteryx has never appeared or mentioned in any Jurassic Park films, it has however appeared in the Dinosaur Field Guide as well as the Jurassic World Dinosaur Field Guide.

entities.name: Centrosaurus
entities.description:
is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur from the Campanian age of Late Cretaceous Canada. Their remains have been found in the Dinosaur Park Formation, dating from 76.5 to 75.5 million years ago.

Like other centrosaurines, Centrosaurus had a single large horn over the nose. Centrosaurus could reach a length of 6 meters. Many dozens of skeletons are have been identified. In some cases, hundreds of individuals scattered bones have been found; likely as evidence of a mass drowning, in what must have been stampedes across torrentially charged and dangerously stormy rivers in migrational crossings gone wrong. Centrosaurus lived with Albertosaurus, Chasmosaurus, Chirostenotes, Corythosaurus, Daspletosaurus, Deinosuchus, Dromaeosaurus, Edmontonia, Euoplocephalus, Lambeosaurus, Ornithomimus, Parasaurolophus, Scolosaurus, Stegoceras, Struthiomimus, and Styracosaurus.

Centrosaurus appeared in the Dinopedia section of the website Jurassic Park Institute. The image shows two Centrosaurus fighting for mates.

Centrosaurus is nr. 099 of the Herbivore Twos that can be created in Jurassic Park III: Park Builder.

Ceramagnus appears in the game as an apex resilient dinosaur and a raid boss.

entities.name: Ceratops
entities.description:
is a dubious genus of ceratopsian dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Judith River Formation in Montana, the United States. While the genus is poorly known in medias, Ceratops was an important dinosaur in the history of dinosaurs as it is the type genus for which both the Ceratopsia and the Ceratopsidae have been named.

Ceratops is one of the created dinosaurs that could be found in the nursery of the Jurassic Park Discovery Center of the Islands of Adventure.

entities.name: Ceratosaurus
entities.description:
was a medium-sized carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived at the same time as the larger Allosaurus, in the Late Jurassic period. However, it also lived some millions of years before the emergence of the successful allosauroids, being of the more primitive four fingered Ceratosauria. What makes it different and distinctive is the large horn on top of its nose and the two horns over its eyes. The use of it has been debated and is most likely used for display (it can be hypothesized that keratinor soft tissue covered the horns), a weapon, or a special used for courtship battles. About 100 years ago, when it was first discovered, it was one of the most well-known dinosaurs. Other unusual features is that Ceratosaurus had a row of osteoderms running along its spine to the tail and four fingers on its hands, instead of the more common three among the other large meat-eaters during its time. This is typically an indication that this theropod is relatively primitive, whose ancestral relatives are from the earlier times of the Mid Triassic to Mid Jurassic periods when coelophysoideans and ceratosaurians were much more prevalent. Allosaurids and megalosaurian carnosaurs, both kinds tetanurans, were much more advanced, with greater speed and intelligence, as well as the ability in at least allosaurids to form packs.

It is probable that the Ceratosaurus ended up being sidelined by the Allosaurus in North America, as evidenced by the fact that Ceratosaurus is the rarest fossil theropod genus present in the magnificent Cleveland Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry. It probably became a prowler of the forest, using its terrifying dentition when ambushing smaller dinosaurs.

This information is given about Ceratosaurus in Jurassic Park: Explorer:

Ceratosaurus, like other theropods cloned by InGen, exhibited pronated wrists. There were two distinct variants of the cloned Ceratosaurus. One variant had a bright red head and a white body with black striping, while the other variant was a monotone gray color. The only known individual observed had small horns over its eyes, resembling those of a Ceratosaurus juvenile. Interestingly, it also possessed a longer and more pointed nasal horn, similar to that of a Triceratops, as opposed to the rounded bump-like horn seen in the original Ceratosaurus.

entities.description:
is a genus spinosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian) of Britain.

The animal was named in 2021 alongside another spinosaurid called and its name means "horned crocodile face", with the species name inferodios meaning "hell heron".

Ceratosuchops was among the animals in the Jurassic World: Chaos Theory toyline that were added to the app on October 31, 2024.

Ceratosuchops featured in the Epic Evolution toy line. This is not only its first appearance in Jurassic Park franchise as a toy or as a whole, but also its first ever appearance in the media.

entities.name: Cetiosauriscus
entities.description:
(meaning "whale-lizard-like") is an extinct genus of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda sauropod] dinosaur that lived in England during the Middle Jurassic period around 168 to 163 million years ago.

Cetiosauriscus is a large, long-necked dinosaur found in Europe. Discovered over 100 years ago, there is still a question as to which family of dinosaurs it belongs. This large plant-eater could have been related to either the North American Diplodocus or the Asian Mamenchisaurus. Since Europe was about in the middle of these two continents, perhaps it was related to both!

Adding to the mystery of this dinosaur, no skull material has yet been found with any of the five partial skeletons discovered to date. It has gone through several name changes and there are currently four species attributed to the genus, spanning more than 20 million years of the Jurassic. It is expected that it will be studied and possibly reassigned in the future.

Cetiosauriscus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Cetiosaurus
entities.description:
was a large sauropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic period. Its name means 'whale lizard'. It was named by Sir Richard Owen. It was initially thought to be an ancient crocodilian, and was though later proven not to be and included in the then new classification coined by the brilliant but flawed Owen, Dinosauria, named under the assumption it was not a dinosaur. Its huge size was exciting to the Victorians - after all, this was the first ever sauropod found and named. It lived where England is today, some 168 million years ago. It grew to 16 metres and would have weighed 12 tons; the largest land animal ever that the early paleontologists knew of, before larger sauropods were found elsewhere in the world and even in Britain again (Brachiosaurids recently found on the Isle of Wight for instance) Cetiosaurus was a taste of things to come; truly titanic prehistoric animals for all to see and the experts to study. It is perhaps only the sixth dinosaur ever to be named, after Megalosaurus (1st), Iguanodon (2nd), etc.

Cetiosaurus gives its name to the Cetiosauridae, which represent a relatively primitive Sauropod line, which is understandable considering their heyday was well within the Mid Jurassic. They are evolutionarily more advanced than the even earlier forms such as the Vulcanodontidae, but are certainly less advanced than the Diplodocids, Camarasaurids, and Brachiosaurids.

Cetiosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

Cetiosaurus is number 48 of the Herbivore Twos that can be created in the game Jurassic Park III: Park Builder.

entities.name: Chaoyangsaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Chaoyang lizard") is an extinct genus of marginocephalian ceratopsian dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Jurassic period. It is a very important member of the family of horned dinosaurs because it shows they lived during the Jurassic period. Before the discovery of this little dinosaur, it was believed that the ceratopsians first showed up in the Cretaceous period. This early family member lived before Protoceratops and Psittacosaurus, which are considered some of the earliest members of this family. Like the other early family members, Chaoyangsaurus is also from Asia.

First discovered in the early 1980's, rumors of this dinosaur floated around the paleontological community until it was formally described in 1999. It had previously been known by a somewhat different spelling, Chaoyoungosaurus, but its formal description changed that. This dinosaur seems to show an evolutionary link between the ceratopsian dinosaurs and the heterodontosauridae.

Chaoyangsaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Chasmosaurus
entities.description:
was the oldest of the long-frilled, horned ceratopsian dinosaurs, whose family includes Triceratops. It was a medium-sized plant-eater that had a long neck frill with large holes in the bone and narrow structures to support the weight of the frill. It would have had skin stretched over the holes in its frill. Chasmosaurus had medium-sized horns over its eyes, and a smaller nose horn.

Judging from the monotypic bone beds of the Chasmosaurus fossils, this animal traveled in single species herds. Since the frill of a Chasmosaurus would not be a very effective defensive weapon, there is speculation that it may have been used for identification and attracting mates. New discoveries suggest the possibility that Chasmosaurus and Pentaceratops might belong in the same genus.

Centrosaurus is briefly seen in the Jurassic Park: Paint and Activity Center story "The Park" alongside other certopsians related to Triceratops.

Chasmosaurus is one of the dinosaurs that can be cloned in Jurassic Park III: Park Builder. It is no. 097 of the Herbivore Twos.

entities.name: Chebsaurus
entities.description:
("cheb lizard"), also referred as the giant of Ksour, is a genus of cetiosaurid sauropod that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now Algeria. It is the first dinosaur to be described from Algeria, as well as the most complete sauropod from this country. Its remains were found in the Callovian-aged Aïssa Formation.

Discovered in 1999 by the company Sonatrach, it was named in 2005. The word cheb is colloquial arabic for "young man", because the bones were believed to be from a juvenile at first. Chebsaurus was compared to its relatives, Cetiosaurus and Lapparentosaurus, for examination.

Chebsaurus is featured in a news from the defunct Jurassic Park Institute. It is outdatedly being referred to as a diplodocid from the Late Jurassic period, as this was made before 2005, the year where it was fully described.

While it isn't precise, the article mentions that the sauropod fossils were discovered by the company Sonatrach, which did happen to stumble upon the remains of Chebsaurus, as you can see [https://naama.mta.gov.dz/en/dinosaur-museum/ here] or [https://www.facebook.com/groups/136927823164630/posts/891041781086560/ there].

entities.name: Chelsea
entities.description:
Chelsea was a model of a genetically modified Triceratops created by Joe Laudati. The model was a partner model to the Robertosaurus Rex. It was a concept for an unproduced Jurassic Park toyline that would have involved "nastier" dinosaurs fighting against soldiers with "dino-fighting" gear and vehicles. The client for the model was Robert Yee. The original model was created in Feburary 2006.

A week after the Robertosaurus Rex was created, Robert asked for a Triceratops model to go with it. Joe designed the Triceratops based off of the original Jurassic Park design, but made it look angrier. The Triceratops was bred to be deep blue and purple and had a meaner temperament. Chelsea was never given a species name. Joe stated, "We didn’t have a ‘species name’ but I guess it would be triceratops horridus." Ultimately, the model never went into production in the toyline.

The molds of the Triceratops were later used to make resin castings for model kits, which were sold. In December 2025, Joe stated that he still had a model of the Triceratops.

entities.name: Chicken
entities.description:
The (Gallus gallus domesticus or Gallus domesticus) is a large and round short-winged bird, domesticated from the (Gallus gallus) of Southeast Asia around 8,000 years ago. Most chickens are raised for food, providing meat and eggs; others are kept as pets or for cockfighting.

Chickens are common and widespread domestic animals, with a total population of 26.5 billion as of 2023, and an annual production of more than 50 billion birds. A hen bred for laying can lay over 300 eggs per year. There are numerous cultural references to chickens in folklore, religion, and literature.

A chicken was present in a restaurant within Costa Rica when Lewis Dodgson encounters Dennis Nedry.

Sarr's lab is hidden under a chicken farm. When the Nublar Six and Zayna arrives at the location, Sammy remarks the "cute" chickens.

entities.description:
is an extinct genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now China, found within the formation of Ulanshuai. Its classification is unsure, but it is considered that it may be a neovenatorid. There is only one species, C. tashuikouensis, being described by Hu in 1964. The name of this dinosaur comes from the Jilantai Salt Lake, where the species was discovered.

Chilantaisaurus is an obtainable dinosaur from the Jurassic World: Rebirth collection.

Chilantaisaurus is mentioned in the entry of Psittacosaurus as its enemy. However, Psittacosaurus lived before Chilantaisaurus existed.

entities.name: Chindesaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of basal saurischian dinosaur from the Late Triassic (213-210 million years ago) of the southwestern United States. It is known from a single species, C. bryansmalli, based on a partial skeleton recovered from Petrified Forest National Park in Arizona. The original specimen was nicknamed "Gertie", and generated much publicity for the park upon its discovery in 1984 and airlift out of the park in 1985. Other fragmentary referred specimens have been found in Late Triassic sediments throughout Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas, but these may not belong to the genus. Chindesaurus was a bipedal carnivore, approximately as large as a wolf.

Chindesaurus classification is debated, and various papers have had different conclusions on its affinities. Its fossils were originally believed to belong to "prosauropods" (basal sauropodomorphs), but its original description and numerous subsequent papers argued that it was a herrerasaurid or herrerasaurian. A 2019 redescription of its holotype considered Chindesaurus to be a theropod closely related to Tawa, a slightly smaller dinosaur known from the Hayden Quarry of Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.

Chindesaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.

entities.name: Chirostenotes
entities.description:
(meaning "narrow-handed") is an extinct genus of oviraptorosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived in Alberta, Canada during the Late Cretaceous period. It was a small, quick hunter with long slender hands. Since its discovery, Chirostenotes has been put into several different branches of the dinosaur family tree - including the oviraptorid and dromaeosaur families. Currently, it is a part of the caenagnathid family, but that may change once more fossils are uncovered.

This little dinosaur has been the subject of a good amount of study over the years. There were once four species named, but are now separated into their own genus or are synonyms. As a later Cretaceous member of the maniraptorid, it may have been a feathered dinosaur based on current thinking about this family.

Chirostenotes was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its artwork, it is shown chasing a lizard.

Chirostenotes also appeared in the Dinosaur Field Guide, but in the Jurassic World Dinosaur Field Guide it was completely replaced by Anzu.

entities.name: Chlamydosaurus sputori
entities.description:
Chlamydosaurus sputori was a bio-engineered dinosaur species planned to appear in the cut Jurassic Park 4. These "spitters" are large and have the ability to dig, like the Excavaraptor. Dilophosaurus would also be retconned for Chlamydosaurus.

The Dilophosaurus would be retconned as Chlamydosaurus sputori in the John Sayles script of Jurassic Park 4. The ones at Jurassic Park took on prey such as unlucky humans. The Dilophosaurus that killed Dennis Nedry would be a Chlamydosaurus.

For Jurassic Park 4, they would have been used instead of Dilophosaurus. In the abandoned script, they were first seen in a flashback, where one kills Nedry, retconning the Dilophosaurus from the first movie as a member of this species. When Nick arrived at Isla Nublar, he entered the nesting area of the Chlamydosaurus. During his escape, a Chlamydosaurus was caught and eaten by an Excavaraptor. Later, two called Casper and Pollux are seen being trained by Nick, alongside the genetically engineered Deinonychus. In the end of the abandoned script, they escape, killing a man called Pepe. They attempt to attack Nick, but run off into the jungle.

entities.name: Chubutisaurus
entities.description:
(meaning "Chubut lizard") is a genus of dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period. It lived in South America. It is classified as a sauropod, specifically one of the titanosaurs. The type species, Chubutisaurus insignis, was described by del Corro in 1975. Its fossils were found in the Cerro Barcino Formation, Albian stage, about 110 million years ago. Chubutisaurus had a more robust radius than Venenosaurus. In 2010 Gregory Paul gave a length of 18 meters (59 feet) and a weight of 12 tons (13.2 short tons). Thomas Holtz estimated its length at 23 meters (75.5 feet) in 2012.

Chubutisaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. In its artwork, it is shown standing up on its hind legs to eat the leaves at the top of a tree.

Chubutisaurus is mentioned on Dinotracker.com as a prey item of Carnotaurus in the predator’s field guide along with turtles. However, Chubutisaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, while Carnotaurus was from the Late Cretaceous.

It is unknown whether or not this is meant to imply that Chubutisaurus was ever cloned in canon, as every other species mentioned (Mamenchisaurus, Corythosaurus, Pachycephalosaurus, Pachyrhinosaurus and Lystrosaurus) are all known to be active as of 2022. However, it's likely meant to be a simple mention for the description of the Carnotaurus.

entities.name: Chungkingosaurus
entities.description:
is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur. The Chungkingosaurus jiangbeiensis holotype was one of the smallest stegosaurs with a length of less than four metres (about thirteen feet), even though it was apparently an adult, judging by the ossification of the sacrum. Chungkingosaurus sp. 1 was estimated at five metres; Chungkingosaurus sp. 2 was seen as longer than five metres. Chungkingosaurus strongly resembled Tuojiangosaurus, found in the same formation, in many anatomical details. Chungkingosaurus was different in its smaller size, deeper snout and front lower jaws (resulting in a relatively high and narrow skull), and non-overlapping teeth with less pronounced denticles.

Chungkingosaurus probably possessed two rows of plates and spikes on its back, which were arranged in pairs, but the total number is unknown. A skeleton model in the Chongqing Municipal museum shows fourteen pairs of plates. This model also has two pairs of tail spikes. The plates of Chungkingosaurus have a thickened middle section, as if they were modified spikes. The plates resemble those of Tuojiangosaurus. The form of the thagomizer, the tail end spikes used as a defensive weapon, is only known from specimen CV 00208. It preserves two pairs of obliquely vertical, rather stout, spikes. A third pair to the front of these was originally present but lost during the excavation. A unique feature is the presence of an additional pair at the very tail end, consisting of long thin spikes oriented almost horizontally and obliquely to the sides and rear in top view. Paul described this kind of thagomizer as a "pin-cushion array". The thagomizer of Tuojiangosaurus is not known from articulated remains.

entities.name: Citipes
entities.description:
(not to be confused with Citipati) is a genus of caenagnathid that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Alberta, Canada. Only one species has been assigned to this dinosaur: Citipes elegans.

Like Caenagnathus, it has a convoluted taxonomic history; it has been previously assigned to the genera Ornithomimus, Macrophalangia (a synonym of Chirostenotes), Elmisaurus, Chirostenotes, and before being given its own genus in 2020. The identification of several autapomorphies allow Citipes to be distinguished from its contemporaries and its closely related genera.

The specimens belonging to Citipes comes from the Dinosaur Park formation, a geological dig site renowned for famous dinosaurs like Styracosaurus and Parasaurolophus.

Citipes is indirectly mentioned in the description of Elmisaurus in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute. The website refers to a species of Elmisaurus from North America that some scientists believe that it is actually Chirostenotes. This is referring to Elmisaurus elegans, who has been recognised as the new genus Citipes in 2020.

entities.name: Claosaurus
entities.description:
is an extinct genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period (Santonian-Campanian) in what is now the USA. It was named after the odd position of the fossils when discovered.

Traditionally classified as an early member of the family Hadrosauridae, a 2008 analysis found Claosaurus agilis to be outside of the clade containing Hadrosaurus and other hadrosaurids, making it the closest non-hadrosaurid relative of true hadrosaurids within the clade Hadrosauria.

Claosaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia. It did not receive a dino card, instead being redirected to Edmontosaurus as the genus is no longer considered valid. However, Claosaurus is considered a valid dinosaur nowaday.

Timothy Bradley made an illustration of Claosaurus, even though it wasn't used.

entities.name: Coelophysis
entities.description:
is a very well known early dinosaur as scientists have discovered hundreds of skeletons of this meat-eater. It is the oldest dinosaur known in North America, living around 216 to 203 million years ago, during the Late Triassic Period. It was a swift hunter that seemed to eat almost anything it could catch, including small dinosaurs, small mammals, small reptiles, lizards, and fish. Some of the skeletons found in New Mexico had the remains of what appeared to be smaller Coelophysis in their stomachs, suggesting it occasionally resorted to cannibalism. It wasn't until in 2002 that the remains from the Ghost Ranch specimens have been re-examined, and later concluded that the "juvenile coelophysids" found in the abdominal cavities were actually from small crurotarsan reptiles such as Hesperosuchus. This is likely the result of the fossil of a larger individual overlapping a smaller one.

Coelophysis could get fairly large for an early dinosaur, with adults ranging to a size of up to 3 m (10 feet). These sizes are generally divided into two specimen types - robust and gracile - and are thought to represent gender differentiation. Being a basal (one of the first) theropods, it had some characteristics which were lost on later members of the theropod family. It still had four fingers, although the fourth digit was quite small.

The remains of hundreds of individuals were found at Ghost Ranch in New Mexico, which provided scientists with an unprecedented opportunity to study the individual differences within a large herd of the same dinosaurs.

Like other early carnivores, Coelophysis had many small, sharp teeth. As is shown by the vast numbers of individuals at Ghost Ranch, it is evident that early dinosaurs exhibited social behavior to the extent of congregating in large packs. The exact purpose of this large gathering is not known, but some scientists feel that it may have been breeding season.

entities.name: Coelurosaurus
entities.description:
"Coelurosaurus" is a small, herbivorous dinosaur mentioned within the novel Jurassic Park. While it's true identity remains unknown, it has been suggested to be a misspelling of either Coelurus or [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Coelosaurus%22_antiquus Coelosaurus] and a mistaken name by Henry Wu, as he said he wasn't sure that was correct.

Coelurosaurus is described to be a small herbivore by Dr. Henry Wu, but aside from that, there is next-to-no other information given about it. It is commonly theorised to be a mistranslation of Coelurus, a small carnivorous theropod from the Morrison Formation. There are several reasons why this may be the case; the first of which is that Coelurus was present at a fossil formation that InGen was sending expeditions to, meaning that there is a high chance that InGen might have collected their DNA. Coelurus is also present within the film franchise, much like several other novel species. Additionally, of the two most likely candidates behind Coelurusaurus' identity, Coelurus is the only valid one, as [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%22Coelosaurus%22_antiquus Coelosaurus] is considered a dubious Ornithomimid. However, the description of "small herbivore" best fits Coelosaurus. It always possible, however, that "coelurosaurus" could refer to any coelurosaur, as coelurosaurs are the clade containing all Megaraptorans, Tyrannosauroids, Ornithomimosaurs, Maniraptorans (including birds).

Sometime prior to 1989, DNA presumed to belong to a "Coelurosaurus" was acquired by InGen, and the animal was planned to be cloned for Jurassic Park on Isla Nublar. An egg designated as "xxxx-0001/1" being shown to the Endorsement Team by Dr Henry Wu shortly before the incident on the island. It is unknown if the egg hatched before the island was abandoned. However, even if it did, all dinosaurs on Isla Nublar were killed off during the Costa Rican Napalm Strike several hours later.

entities.name: Coelurus
entities.description:
Coelurus would have preferred small, easily captured prey. It is possible that it was shy and avoided contact with heavier animals, as it could not have been very strong. It is quite likely that its preferred escape method would have been a rapid retreat from any threat. Coelurus was likely adapted for hunting small prey. Due to its small size, it may have been predated by larger dinosaurs.

There is still discussion among researchers as to the identification of the type specimen. The most recent detailed study suggests that the four specimens, which were found in the same quarry site, are actually just one individual. It was also once suggested that Coelurus and Ornitholestes was the same creature, but a recent study concluded that they are in fact separate genera. Coelurus is one of the fastest dinosaurs ever known.

Coelurus appears on the Jurassic Park Institute. It is light green in color, and is shown chasing after an unidentified lizard.

Coelurus was cloned by Masrani Global Corporation for their theme park, Jurassic World. The attraction the dinosaur resided is unknown.

entities.description:
is an extinct genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Late Triassic in what is now Argentina. Interestingly, Coloradisaurus lives with its relatives Lessemsaurus as well another prosauropod of a different branch, Riojasaurus. This dinosaur is known from two collected specimens from the Los Colorados Formation, which is where it got its name. It was also one of the dinosaurs to be discovered and named by paleontologist José Bonaparte.

Coloradisaurus is illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, but hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.

entities.name: Amber Clave Night Market
entities.description:
The Amber Clave Night Market, also known as the Amber Clave Underground Market, is an illegal market of prehistoric creatures located in the catacombs of Valletta, Malta.

The underground market is the central hub for the dinosaur black market in the world. Various dinosaurs are sold illegally here. Locusts and lampreys are served as food, dinosaur eggs, and handbags made of dinosaur pelts are also sold in the black market.

The market was set up by Lewis Dodgson and Biosyn who sold it to Soyona Santos as a part of their new partnership.

After Maisie and Blue's daughter, Beta, are taken by Biosyn's hired guns, Owen Grady, Claire Dearing and Barry Sembène track them to Malta, where they discover a dinosaur illegal market that was secretly created by Lewis Dodgson. As Claire and Owen disrupt the market, dinosaurs are unintentionally released, causing havoc. As Owen interrogated Delacourt who was later killed during the chaos, Claire incapacitates and interrogates Biosyn ally Soyona Santos, who reveals that Maisie and Beta are being transported to Biosyn’s headquarters in Italy's Dolomites mountain range. While at the market, they meet Kayla Watts, a sympathetic pilot who delivers the live cargo for market vendors and has access to Biosyn HQ. Later after the incident, the market presumably shut down.

entities.name: Amber Mines
entities.description:
The Amber Mines are located under Biosyn's valley at the Dolomites Mountain range of Italy.

Not much is known about the mines, but as the name suggests, they offer amber to Biosyn, which is used for obtaining prehistoric DNA. The mines are connected through tunnels. Dimetrodon are known to live in those mines.

When Alan Grant, Ellie Sattler, and Maisie escape through the hyperloop train, the transport is stopped, unbeknownst to them, by Lewis Dodgson. Grant opens the door, and they find themselves in the mines and try to find a way out. While trying to find a way out, they are attacked by Dimetrodons.

When they find an exit, the gate is locked. However, Ian Malcolm shows up and tries to unlock it by trying different codes. Back at the control room, Ramsay looks to a security camera and sees the predicament and proceeds to type in a code that unlocked the gate right when Ian pressed the code he thought was right.

entities.name: Animal Kingdom
entities.description:
Animal Kingdom was a pioneering wildlife park established by John Hammond in 1969 in Nairobi, Kenya. It served as Hammond’s initial attempt at combining the excitement of exotic animal attractions with the burgeoning possibilities of genetic science. The park focused primarily on showcasing living dinosaurs created through early genetic cloning techniques, representing one of the first steps toward what would later become the ambitious Jurassic Park project.

The park was managed by Robert Muldoon, who served as the game warden. Muldoon’s experience in Animal Kingdom provided him with essential knowledge about managing genetically resurrected prehistoric creatures, skills he later brought to Jurassic Park. Animal Kingdom’s success and challenges helped shape Hammond’s vision and operational strategies for his subsequent theme parks.

Though less technologically advanced than Jurassic Park, Animal Kingdom was instrumental in proving the viability of de-extinction through genetic manipulation. It laid the groundwork for future developments in dinosaur cloning and park design. Its establishment in Nairobi, Kenya, was strategically chosen for its rich biodiversity and suitable environment for housing large exotic animals, including the cloned dinosaurs.

The name "Animal Kingdom" is likely inspired by Disney's Animal Kingdom at Walt Disney World in Florida, reflecting a trend toward immersive wildlife-themed parks. This connection hints at the cultural influence and public fascination with animal-themed entertainment venues during the mid-20th century. While fictional, Animal Kingdom symbolizes the intersection of cutting-edge science and entertainment that the Jurassic franchise explores.

entities.name: Antarctica
entities.description:
Antarctica is a continent located in the South Pole surrounded by the Ross Sea and Weddell Sea. It is not only considered to be the coldest and driest continent but also the only one without a permanent human population. Antarctica is home to colonies of penguins (such as the emperor penguin) as well as other animals like the orca, , and Patagonian toothfish. In fact, it is known for its many prehistoric animals like Cryolophosaurus, Glacialisaurus, Antarctopelta, , , and Oreochima.

Kenji Kon asks the Nublar Six whether the plane crashed in Italy or in Antarctica.

Antarctica is mentioned in the Evo Facts section for Antarctopelta and Cryolophosaurus.

It is mentioned in the facts section of Antarctopelta in the game.

entities.name: Argentina
entities.description:
Argentina, officially the Argentine Republic, is a country in the southern half of South America that borders Chile to the west, Bolivia and Paraguay to the north, Brazil to the northeast, and Uruguay to the east. Its capital and largest city is Bueno Aires. It maintains the second-largest economy in South America. Its environment includes part of the Andes mountain range and the plains of the Pampas. This is where the tango dance and famous writer originate from, but also the earliest (Eoraptor, Herrerasaurus, Pisanosaurus) and biggest dinosaurs (Argentinosaurus, Dreadnoughtus, Patagotitan). Argentina hosts numerous geological sites and dinosaurs, with notable ones being Giganotosaurus, Carnotaurus, Amargasaurus, Austroraptor, Saltasaurus, and .

Richard Levine mentions that he thinks that the dinosaur that killed his guide Diego was a Carnotaurus, which originated from the Gorro Frigo formation in Argentina.

Argentina is one of the countries where the visitors from your park come from.

The Glacier Park from the game is revealed to be located inside Argentina, more specifically Patagonia. Argentina also appears in a promotional quiz for the game, on which country Giganotosaurus was discovered (with Argentina being the correct answer).

The name honors Bian and is a reference to the Lufeng Formation (originally formally called Lower Lufeng Series).

Bienosaurus was illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute. However, it hadn’t received a dino card before its closure in 2006, It is it is inaccurately depicted as an ornithopod, despite being a thyreophoran.

entities.name: Australia
entities.description:
Australia, officially the Commonwealth of Australia, is a country located in Oceania neighboring New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Its capital is Canberra. Australia is known for its desert climate and endemic species like the kangaroo, koala, emu, and wombat. However, it is also home to dangerous animals like the saltwater crocodile or the . Some Australian prehistoric animals include Australovenator, Leaellynasaura, Muttaburrasaurus, Procoptodon, Minmi, Thylacoleo, Megalania, and Koolasuchus.

When the Nublar Six arrived in the desert of Mantah Corp Island, Kenji wonders if they are in Australia before Darius corrected him, noting that Australia is too far away for them to have gotten there from Isla Nublar.

By some point in 2022, a population of Stygimoloch and Dimorphodon resided within Australia. According to Dinotracker, a flock of Dimorphodon are seen hanging on a sign in Perth while a sick Stygimoloch is been filmed and shown transported to a sanctuary in Queensland.

Australia is one of the countries where visitors from your park come from.
